items.title: Eval bug: SIGSEGV in `ggml_compute_forward_flash_attn_ext_tiled` (CPU) on long prompts — reproduces across multiple models/commits, workaround is `--flash-attn off`
items.author: fluffyxenia
items.body_excerpt:
### Name and Version

Reproduced on two separate commits, ~3h17m apart in history:
- `8ea290247c87ced2ab245b056ffe96dbcf90d36c` (2026-09-11 21:36:52 +0200)
- `82d6bb284d1ff1c6ef37f29a4c3b63d1a8b11806` (2026-09-12 00:53:07 +0200, fresh `git clone` of `master` at test time)

`ggml_compute_forward_flash_attn_ext_tiled` (`ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ops.cpp`) has not been modified in at least 21 days prior to this report, and none of the file's recent changes relate to flash attention — this does not appear to be a recent regression, including not from the v0.4.0 "sparse flash attention" work (which only touches Metal/CUDA backends and newer DeepSeek-V4/GLM/qwen4exp architectures, not this function).

### Operating systems

Reproduces on: **Android 15 (Termux)**, aarch64, Snapdragon w/ Adreno 810 GPU.

Does **not** reproduce (same steps, same llama.cpp commit, dramatically longer prompts) on:
- Linux x86_64, AMD iGPU (Vega 10, Mesa/RADV)
- Linux aarch64, Raspberry Pi 4, CPU-only

### GGML backends

CPU (crash is identical whether Vulkan support is compiled in or not — reproduced on both a `-DGGML_VULKAN=ON` build and a `-DGGML_VULKAN=OFF` build from the same commit).

### Hardware

Primary repro device: Android phone (Termux), Snapdragon SoC, Adreno 810 GPU, 8GB RAM.

Cross-platform comparison (both completed cleanly with no crash, no garbled output):
- x86_64 desktop, AMD Vega 10 iGPU
- Raspberry Pi 4 (aarch64, CPU-only)

### Models

Reproduces across three different models/architectures on the Android device:
- Qwen3.5-0.8B (Q8_0, BF16, and Q4_K_M quants all affected) — crashes at `task.n_tokens = 350`
- Gemma 4 E2B (QAT Q4_K_XL)
- A custom ~112M-parameter Qwen3-architecture model with a much smaller attention-head configuration — required a much longer prompt (`task.n_tokens = 7180`) to hit the same code path, consistent with the crash threshold being driven by total attention-tile count (heads × sequence length), not by model identity or size alone.

On the two non-Android machines, the same Qwen3.5-0.8B and Gemma 4 E2B files completed successfully at 12,549 and 15,071 prompt tokens respectively (35–43x the Android crash threshold) with no crash and coherent output.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

`llama-server` segfaults (`SIGSEGV`) inside `__memset_aarch64` (Android Bionic libc), called from:

```
#0 __memset_aarch64 (from /apex/com.android.runtime/lib64/bionic/libc.so)
#1 ggml_compute_forward_flash_attn_ext_tiled (params=..., dst=..., ir0=462, ir1=528)
    at ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ops.cpp:8992
#2 ggml_compute_forward_flash_attn_ext_f16 (...) at ops.cpp:9338
#3 ggml_compute_forward_flash_attn_ext (...) at ops.cpp:9356
#4 ggml_compute_forward (...) at ggml-cpu.c:2027
#5 ggml_graph_compute_thread (...) at ggml-cpu.c:3147
#6-8 (OpenMP dispatch)
```

Register state at crash (aarch64 calling convention — `memset(x0, x1, x2)`):
```
x0 (dest) = 0xb400007d47853500
x1 (fill) = 0                     ← zero-fill
x2 (size) = 0xff80 = 65408        ← plausible/sane size, not an obvious overflow
```

The size argument being sane (not a garbage/overflowed value) points to a buffer-size *calculation* mismatch for a specific tile range, rather than an integer-overflow bug — the kernel computes a memset of a reasonable size into a destination that apparently doesn't have that much room, specifically for the tile indexed by `ir0=462, ir1=528` in this reproduction.

The crash occurs on the **first real prompt processing batch** (not during the graph-reservation/warmup pass, which uses synthetic data and never triggers it) — i.e., it's data/shape-dependent, not something a warmup pass can catch.

**Reproduction (any OpenAI-compatible client works; example via curl):**
```
llama-server -m <model.gguf> -np 1 -c <ctx> --host 0.0.0.0
# then send a chat completion with a long enough prompt that the actual
# request's token count crosses the model-specific threshold above
```

**Workaround:** `--flash-attn off` (or `-fa off`) avoids the crash entirely in every test performed. Flash attention is `auto` by default in current versions, so this must be set explicitly — merely omitting an old `-fa on` flag is not sufficient, since `auto` still enables it.

Caveat on scope: `--flash-attn off` also disables quantized KV cache support (`-ctk`/`-ctv`), since that currently only has an implementation through the flash-attention path — so this workaround isn't free for memory-constrained setups that also wanted quantized KV cache.

### Hypothesis on the platform split

The underlying buffer-sizing bug is very likely present on all platforms, but only Android's Scudo allocator (used by Bionic) places guard pages around heap allocations aggressively enough to turn the resulting out-of-bounds write into an immediate, loud crash. glibc-based systems (the two non-Android machines tested) most likely experience the same out-of-bounds write, just landing in adjacent already-allocated heap/scratch memory rather than an unmapped page — consistent with why output stayed coherent there rather than showing corruption (flash attention's tiled implementation reuses scratch/accumulator buffers heavily across tile iterations, so an overflow into adjacent scratch space that's about to be overwritten by the next tile anyway would plausibly have no visible effect).

### Related but distinct issue

While investigating this on Termux, we also hit the already-reported, still-open Vulkan shader compile issue [#28234](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/28234) (`Invalid capability operand: 5447` in the coopmat2 shaders) — that's a separate build-time bug in the Vulkan shader-generation path, unrelated to this CPU-backend runtime segfault (confirmed unrelated by reproducing this issue on a `-DGGML_VULKAN=OFF` build, which never invokes glslc/shaderc at all).

### First Bad Commit

_No response_ — not a recent regression as far as we can determine; see "Name and Version" above.

items.title: [Bug][MP Observability] init_event_bus leaks the previous EventBus drain thread on reinitialization
items.author: adolphinvx
items.body_excerpt:
**Label**

`bug`, `mem_leak`, `mp_mode`

**Describe the bug**

`init_event_bus()` replaces the process-local observability `EventBus` singleton without stopping the previous instance.

If the previous bus has already been started, its background drain thread remains alive after replacement. Repeated initialization in the same Python process therefore causes the number of live `EventBus` threads to grow linearly.

Because `EventBus.stop()` is not called, the previous bus also does not run its subscriber shutdown hooks.

The normal MP server startup path initializes observability once, so this primarily affects tests, embedded or replay use cases, and any future same-process reconfiguration.

**To Reproduce**

Tested against `origin/dev` at commit `88c482d042d4272671ce4289f76fb9c896a26436`.

```python
import gc
import threading
import weakref

from lmcache.v1.mp_observability.event_bus import (
    EventBusConfig,
    init_event_bus,
)


def live_event_bus_threads() -> int:
    return sum(
        thread.name == "EventBus" and thread.is_alive()
        for thread in threading.enumerate()
    )


baseline = live_event_bus_threads()
old_bus_refs = []

for _ in range(10):
    bus = init_event_bus(EventBusConfig(enabled=True))
    bus.start()
    old_bus_refs.append(weakref.ref(bus))

    init_event_bus(EventBusConfig(enabled=False))

del bus
gc.collect()

print("extra live EventBus threads:", live_event_bus_threads() - baseline)

# Cleanup leaked buses so the reproducer does not leave background threads.
for bus_ref in old_bus_refs:
    old_bus = bus_ref()
    if old_bus is not None:
        old_bus.stop()

print("after cleanup:", live_event_bus_threads() - baseline)
```

Observed output:

```text
extra live EventBus threads: 10
after cleanup: 0
```

**Expected behavior**

Given that `init_event_bus()` is documented to replace the global singleton, it should not silently orphan a running bus.

The previous bus should either be stopped before replacement, or repeated initialization while a bus is running should be explicitly rejected and documented.

**Environment**

- OS: macOS 26.2
- Python: 3.12.11
- LMCache commit: `88c482d042d4272671ce4289f76fb9c896a26436`

**Additional context**

The current implementation directly overwrites the singleton:

```python
_global_bus = EventBus(config)
```

It does not call `stop()` on the previous instance.

I also ran an isolated verification in five independent Python processes, with 20 replacements per process. Each process retained exactly 20 live drain threads, and all threads exited after explicitly stopping the old buses. OpenTelemetry gauge registration was disabled for that verification to isolate the EventBus thread lifecycle.

This report is specifically about the process-local EventBus drain-thread and subscriber lifecycle. It does not require CUDA to reproduce and is not claiming a CUDA resource leak or a KV-cache data-path correctness issue.

I would be happy to work on the fix and regression test if the expected reinitialization semantics are confirmed.

## Motivation

Contributes to #20865.

items.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4 HiCache: SWA host pool is sized from the small SWA device pool, so idle prefixes miss the host tier long before the KV host pool fills
items.author: divyvasal
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

On DeepSeek-V4 with HiCache, the SWA host pool is sized as `device_swa_pages * hicache_ratio`. The SWA device pool is fixed and small: 362,240 tokens on our setup, regardless of `--mem-fraction-static`. As a result, the SWA host pool, about 724K tokens at ratio 2, fills long before the full-KV host pool does.

When `drive_host_eviction` evicts SWA host windows (LRU), conversations that were evicted from device earliest lose the SWA window at every node on their path. Their full KV is still on host: `hicache_host_used_tokens` < total, and `hicache_dropped_tokens_total` = 0. But the SWA match validator (`components/swa.py`, `create_match_validator`) rejects every node, so the match falls back to the root.

The request is then **fully recomputed**:
- `cached_tokens` = 0.
- `prefill_effective_tokens_total{mode="host_hit"}` does not move.
- Nothing is logged.

In practice the host tier stops helping exactly the idle conversations it exists for, once a workload has prefilled more than roughly SWA-host-capacity / window × chunk tokens. On our setup that is about 20M+ fresh tokens. The KV host pool is still mostly empty at that point, so the failure is invisible in the existing HiCache metrics.

### Reproduction

- **sglang:** nightly at `4cbf290f`
- **Model:** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (MXFP4), 4x B300 per replica
- **Flags:** `--tp-size 4 --ep-size 4 --mem-fraction-static 0.60 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 8192 --schedule-policy shortest-prefill-first --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-ratio 2 --hicache-write-policy write_through --enable-cache-report --enable-metrics`

Engine log at startup:

```
DSV4 pool sizes: full=18361088, swa=362240, ...
Allocating 18.22 GB host memory for V4 paged pool 'swa' (layers=43, pages=2830, ...)   # 2830 * 256 = 724,480 SWA host tokens
```

1. Send two ~80K-token prompts (a system document plus a question), temperature 0. Resend them to confirm a device hit.
2. Push N tokens of unique one-shot prompts (~540K tokens each), enough to evict both prompts from device.
3. Resend both prompts.

| Fresh tokens pushed in step 2 | `hicache_backup_tokens_total{pool="swa"}` | full-KV host used / total | Resend result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3.3M (device pool capped at 2M with `--max-total-tokens`) | 210K | 3.3M / 4.0M | **host hit**: cached 79,616/79,631, `load_back_tokens{kv}` +79,616, same answer |
| same + 2 min of churn re-sending its own prompts (61M evicted, 63M loaded back) | 210K | 3.3M / 4.0M | **host hit** |
| same, 420 s idle before resend | 421K | 4.0M / 4.0M | **host hit** |
| ~21M (default 0.60 pool, 18.36M device; DSPARK off to avoid sglang#42465) | **1,335,040** | 21.4M / 36.7M, 0 dropped | **miss**: cached 0 / 80,036, full recompute (2.29 s), host_hit +0 |

The same thing happened under an agentic load test (48 growing ~540K-token conversations, 0.60 pool). After 28M fresh tokens, `backup_tokens_total{pool="swa"}` reached 1.79M against a 724K SWA host pool. Full-KV host was at 27.0M/36.7M with 0 dropped. 24/24 idle conversations (7 to 18 min idle) came back with `cached_tokens` 0 and were fully recomputed.

### Expected

As long as the full KV is on host, a previously cached prefix should come back as a host hit. When SWA host pressure is the limit, we'd expect at least one of:
- the SWA host pool sized from full-KV host capacity (or settable on its own, e.g. `--hicache-swa-ratio`);
- SWA host eviction that prefers windows whose full KV is already gone, or that keeps the window at the deepest backed-up node of each path, since only the last window is needed to resume;
- a metric or log line when a host-backed prefix is rejected for missing SWA state, so the failure is visible.

### Notes

- Relevant code: `mem_cache/hybrid_cache/hybrid_pool_assembler.py` (`swa_host_pages = int(device_swa_pages * ratio)`), `mem_cache/unified_cache/components/swa.py` (`create_match_validator`, `drive_host_eviction`).
- Raising `--hicache-ratio` grows the full-KV host pool too, so it is not a practical workaround at large device pools.
- Related but different: #34562 (bit-exactness of SWA prefix reuse).

items.title: [Bug]: MiniMax-M3 (MXFP8) streaming: generation stops (empty delta, finish_reason=stop) right after reasoning closes, whenever a tool call should follow — non-streaming with identical payload succeeds
items.author: ZhandosSeitkaliyev
items.body_excerpt:
### Your current environment

`collect_env.py` could not be run on this host — no outbound internet access (air-gapped deployment). Manually collected equivalent below.

**Versions**
- vLLM: `0.27.0` (build `vllm-0.27.0-tp4-41db7380`)
- PyTorch: `2.13.0+cu129`
- Transformers: `5.15.0`
- GPU: 4x NVIDIA H200 (143771 MiB), driver `595.58.03`

**Model**
- `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3`
- Quantization: `mxfp8` (NVIDIA ModelOpt MXFP8 checkpoint, `weight_block_size=[1,32]`, MoE via `MarlinMxfp8LinearKernel`/`MARLIN` backend) — vLLM's own startup log flags this format as *"experimental and could change in future"*

**Launch command**
```bash
vllm serve /model --served-model-name MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --block-size 128 --max-model-len 65536 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.93 --tool-call-parser minimax_m3 \
  --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
```



### 🐛 Describe the bug

With `stream: true` and `tools` provided, for requests where the model's reasoning is longer / more hedging before deciding to call a tool, the SSE stream **stops immediately after the reasoning block closes**: the next chunk has an empty `delta` and `finish_reason: "stop"`. Nothing is generated after that — no content, no `tool_calls`. This is not a parsing failure; generation itself halts.

The byte-identical payload sent with `"stream": false` succeeds reliably (tested 6/6).

> **Note:** only reproduced so far on an MXFP8-quantized checkpoint (NVIDIA ModelOpt format). Untested whether an unquantized bf16 checkpoint is also affected.

**Minimal repro**

Flat 2-field tool schema — confirmed tool schema complexity/count is not the trigger (fails the same way with 1 tool or 5 tools):

```python
import requests

payload = {
    "model": "MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3",
    "stream": True,
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "сделай docx с названием test и текстом привет"}],
    "tools": [{
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
            "name": "generate_docx_report",
            "description": "Generate a Word document from content.",
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "filename": {"type": "string"},
                    "content": {"type": "string"},
                },
                "required": ["filename", "content"],
            },
        },
    }],
    "tool_choice": "auto",
}

r = requests.post("http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions", json=payload, stream=True)
for line in r.iter_lines():
    if line:
        print(line.decode())
```

**Expected**

Reasoning closes, then either visible content or a populated `tool_calls` delta follows — same as the non-streaming response to the identical payload (`"stream": False` above).

**Observed**

After the last reasoning chunk, the stream emits one more chunk with an empty delta and `finish_reason: "stop"`, then ends. Nothing else is generated.

**Ruled out**
- Tool schema size — reproduces with both a minimal flat 2-field schema and a real ~2KB docstring-heavy schema
- Tool count — 1 tool vs 5 tools, same result
- Payload size in general — byte-identical payloads, only `stream` differs

**Correlation observed (not confirmed causal)**

Requests where the model's own reasoning is short/decisive stream through fine. Requests where reasoning is longer with self-correction (*"But I should check... Actually... Let me reconsider..."*) reliably hit the halt.

**Current workaround**

Routing tool-decision through a separate non-streaming call instead of native streaming tool-calling (application-level, not a real fix — costs 2x LLM calls per turn).



### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug There are two related problems when a streaming delta contains multiple tokens: - When `` and the first reasoning token arrive in the same delta, `deepseek_r1`, `ernie45`, `holo2`, and `step3p5` on 0.28.0 leak the marker into `reasoning_content`. Current `main` also affects `hy_v4`. Non-streaming parsing strips the marker correctly. - When the entire output arrives in one delta, `olmo3` extracts the reasoning but returns an empty `content`, dropping everything after ``. The first issue is in `BaseThinkingReasoningParser.extract_reasoning_streaming` in `vllm/reasoning/basic_parsers.py`: the branch handling both markers strips them, while the start-only branch returns the delta unchanged: ```python elif self.start_token_id in delta_token_ids: if self.end_token_id in delta_token_ids: ...strip... else: return DeltaMessage(reasoning=delta_text) # <-- NOT stripped ``` Token-at-a-time tests do not expose either problem because the marker arrives in its own delta. Multi-token deltas can occur with speculative decoding or grouped streaming output. ### Reproduction ```python # pip install vllm==0.28.0 — CPU only (downloads Qwen3-0.6B tokenizer), exit 1 = bug import logging, warnings logging.disable(logging.CRITICAL); warnings.filterwarnings("ignore") from transformers import AutoTokenizer from vllm.reasoning import ReasoningParserManager as RM TOK = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B") TOK.add_tokens(["", ""], special_tokens=True) ids = TOK.encode("step one", add_special_tokens=False) p = RM.get_reasoning_parser("deepseek_r1")(TOK) d = p.extract_reasoning_streaming("", "step one", "step one",

comments.author: apex-mochen
comments.body:
I re-measured both halves of this on current `main` with the Qwen3-0.6B tokenizer, and both reproduce as described. Three things that matter for whoever lands the fix, since #55210 and #56262 are both open against this:

**1. The defect has three independent copies, and neither open PR reaches all of them.** Both PRs patch exactly `basic_parsers.py` + `olmo3_reasoning_parser.py`. That does fix `deepseek_r1`, `step3p5` and `hy_v3` — all three call `super().extract_reasoning_streaming()` and only re-branch when `start_token_id not in delta_token_ids`, so the base-class change reaches them. It does not reach:

- `ernie45_reasoning_parser.py` — never calls `super()`; it is a standalone reimplementation of the same four-way branch, ending in the identical `else: return DeltaMessage(reasoning=delta_text)`.
- `hy_v4_reasoning_parser.py` — `HYV4ReasoningExtractor` is a standalone class (the parser only adapts it) carrying its own copy: `elif self.start_token_id in delta_token_ids: ... else: return ReasoningDelta(reasoning=delta_text, content=None)`.

So after either PR, `ernie45` still leaks the marker, and `hy_v4` still does on any path where the start token is emitted rather than prompt-injected.

**2. Two in-tree parsers already get this right by construction**, which may be the better pattern to copy than patching branches: `k2_horizon` keeps a text buffer and strips the start token in `_strip_stream_start()`, and `minimax_m3` derives its deltas from `_visible_segments(previous_text/current_text)` so it never hands raw `delta_text` back. Neither cares how many tokens a delta carries.

**3. The live-repro blocker in the report is only half the story.** The report says a server-level witness wasn't possible because the marker always arrives in its own delta. I checked the other half — whether the marker is even visible in `output.text` — and it is:

- `<think>` (id 151667) is in `tokenizer.get_added_vocab()` but **not** in `all_special_tokens`, so vLLM's skip-special check at `vllm/tokenizers/detokenizer_utils.py:36` (`token in set(tokenizer.all_special_tokens)`) does not drop it. Feeding `["<think>","step","one"]` through `_convert_tokens_to_string_with_added_encoders(..., skip_special_tokens=True)` returns `'<think>step one'`.
- So `delta_text` does carry the marker at server defaults, and the only thing between this and a live repro is a step that accepts the marker together with a neighbour — the spec-decode timing the report already identifies.

That difference also makes the two open patches behave differently in the *inverse* shape — a marker that is a genuine special token, so the text has it stripped while `delta_token_ids` still holds the id. There `delta_text.find(start_token)` is `-1`: #55210 guards it (`if start_index >= 0 else delta_text`), #56262 does not, and `delta_text[start_index + len("<think>"):]` becomes `delta_text[6:]`. Measured with `delta_text="step one"` that yields `"ne"` — it silently eats the first `len(start_token) - 1` characters of the first reasoning delta.

**On the `olmo3` half**, the mechanism is an early `return` inside `process_buffer()`'s `end_think_idx > 0` branch, which preempts the `state == CONTENT` flush below it; the trailing text stays in `self.buffer`, and the caller's recovery path is gated on `delta_message is None` so it cannot fire. Confirmed: streaming one delta gives `(reasoning='PRIVATE', content=None)` while `extract_reasoning` gives `('PRIVATE', 'PUBLIC')`. Since the text is retained rather than destroyed, the symptom is really "the tail is delayed by one chunk, and lost if no further delta arrives".

Worth coordinating before both land: #48160 deletes `olmo3_reasoning_parser.py` entirely (−317) and moves this parser onto the streaming engine, and its thread already covers this symptom.

comments.author: halilergul1
comments.body:
I reproduced the ernie45 and hy_v4 halves on current main (6ad2e06c4) with the ERNIE tokenizer and a synthetic HY4 vocab: with deltas `["<think>reasoning words", "</think>", "answer words"]`, streaming returns `reasoning='<think>reasoning words'` while non-streaming returns `'reasoning words'`. In hy_v4 there is a second effect: if the start token id is in the delta but its text was skipped, the start/end-in-one-delta branch slices from `find() == -1` and the reasoning text is lost.

Since #55210 and #56262 only touch `basic_parsers.py` and olmo3, I opened #60195 limited to `ernie45_reasoning_parser.py` and `hy_v4_reasoning_parser.py` (strip the marker text when the start id is in the delta, guard the `find() == -1` case) plus regression tests for both, so the three PRs stay non-overlapping. @LOGO127, if your local follow-up already covers these two files, tell me and I will close mine.

items.title: [RFC]: Bound frontend drain latency for bulk aborts and long non-streaming completions
items.author: aoshen02
items.body_excerpt:
> **Revision 2026-10-07.** This RFC was rewritten around a model of where the time and > memory of an RL `pause(mode="abort")` go, and the PR stacks that follow from it. The previous > text is preserved verbatim in a comment below and in > [`history-original-rfc.md`](https://github.com/aoshen02/vllm/blob/rfc57479/docs/rfc-57479/history-original-rfc.md); its GPU evidence is > summarised in §9. Long derivations, full tables and reproduction commands are on the fork > branch [`aoshen02/vllm@rfc57479/docs`](https://github.com/aoshen02/vllm/tree/rfc57479/docs/rfc-57479), together with the > measurement harness ([`harness/`](https://github.com/aoshen02/vllm/tree/rfc57479/docs/rfc-57479/harness)). # 0. TL;DR An RL trainer pauses generation with `POST /pause?mode=abort` before a weight update, and then needs every partial rollout back. With long outputs and top-k logprobs, the default `/inference/v1/generate` response is several GB per request. Both frontends spend most of the post-pause time building and serialising it. The Python frontend can also run out of memory before the pause. We model the cost per (position, top-k slot) entry, derive which terms dominate, and propose two independent PR stacks, one per frontend. Each stack has one default-format change (same bytes as today) and one opt-in compact format for RL. **Workload:** 32 non-streaming requests in flight, 16,384 input tokens, 245,760 output tokens each, top-128 logprobs, aborted together. DP8 with one mock engine per rank and the real `DPCoordinatorProc`; EP8 is engine-side and not modelled by the CPU mock. Times are seconds from the pause until the client has parsed every response. Memory is the frontend peak RSS: per process for Python (32 API servers on one node), total for Rust (one process). | n = 32, DP8 | Base `0fd2e8d503` | Python stack | Rust stack | |---|---|---|---| | **Default format** (bytes identical to base) | Python: **FAIL**, node memory floor after ~8 min at 36 GiB per process [S2]
Rust: **32.9–33.2 s**, **199–202 GiB** [S2][S3] | **21.3 s**, **9.5 GiB** per process (round-24 tip, two build threads [S27]); 21.6 s / 6.0 GiB with one thread [S7] | **20.73 s**, **14.47 GiB** [S4] | | **RL compact format** (opt-in) | not available | **1.80 s**, **2.0 GiB** per process [S7] | **1.85 s**, **11.86 GiB** [S5] | | Response size per request | Python 2,199.6 MB, Rust 3,408.7 MB [S7][S6] | default 2,199.6 MB; compact 337.0 MB | default 3,408.7 MB; compact 337.0 MB | At bs = 256, base Rust aborted on a failed 4 GiB allocation (measured at DP4 [S20]), and the base storage path fails at DP8 at the node memory floor [S8] (base Python itself was not run at bs = 256). Both stacks complete: RL compact 10.87 s (Python) and 10.91 [10.88–10.97] s (Rust, measured on the previous Rust tip; see §5 for why this carries over) with the official 8-core client, which is the limit there [S7][S3]. **Proposed PRs.** All are on base `0fd2e8d503`. They are drafts in the submitter's fork for review; nothing is opened against `vllm-project/vllm` yet. | # | Frontend | PR | Product LOC (+/−) | Tests | Depends on | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | P1 | Python | [Frontend-only sample-logprobs container hook](https://github.com/aoshen02/vllm/pull/109) | +301 / −13 | +715 | — | | P2 | Python | [Public APIs for generate endpoint plugins](https://github.com/aoshen02/vllm/pull/110): `start_generate`, `replace_route` | +261 / −20 | +434 | stacked on P1 for review order (no code dependency) | | P3 | Python | [generate: keep sample logprobs as engine rows, render without objects](https://github.com/aoshen02/vllm/pull/111) | +871 / −34 | +495 | P1 (code); stacked on P2 | | — | Python | [`vllm-rl-compact` endpoint plugin](https://github.com/aoshen02/vllm/pull/112) (out of tree, not proposed for merge) | 0 in `vllm/` (+1,443 under `plugins/`) | +2,682 | P1–P3 | | R-A | Rust | [server: stream the default generate body from the request runtime](https://github.com/aoshen02/vllm/pull/107) | +380 / −46 | +496 | — | | R-B | Rust | [server: opt-in compact logprobs format for raw generate](https://github.com/aoshen02/vllm/pull/108) | +241 / −13 | +400 / −1 | R-A | **Merge order:** Rust R-A → R-B. Python P1 → P2 → P3; the plugin is released separately once P1 and P2 are in. The two stacks are independent. Two Rust changes with mock-only gains are kept as backup branches and are not proposed (§4). # 1. Problem and scope **The operation.** In RL training the rollout manager calls `pause(mode="abort")` on every API server before each weight sync. Engines abort the running requests and the frontends return each partial completion with `finish_reason="abort"`. The trainer cannot start the update until it has all partials, so the time from the pause to the last parsed response is on the critical path of every training step. The pause/resume API is from RFC #32103. **The workload.** It is the shape of our production RL rollout: - 245,760 output tokens per request, top-128 logprobs, 16,384-token input, non-streaming; - DP8 EP8, n = 32 per frontend node in the main cells and bs = 256 in the cohort cells; - `ignore_eos`, no stop strings, no prompt logprobs. **What RL needs from each response:** the output `token_ids`, and for every position the top-k token ids and their float32 logprobs. It does not need text, decoded token strings, the sampled slot or ranks. **Out of scope:** - **R3 (routed experts):** deferred by the submitter. The default `routed_experts` path is unchanged. - **Streaming:** RL here uses non-streaming requests. Streaming default responses are unchanged; the compact format rejects `stream: true` with 400 in Rust. Python compact streaming lives only in the out-of-tree plugin. - Engine-side pause semantics and DP consensus are unchanged. # 2. items.title: [Feature]: Shared per choice `ChatStreamProcessor` for chat serving and streaming derender
items.author: hickeyma
items.body_excerpt:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

Tracking issue for a follow up from the #50550 review, where @sagearc asked whether streaming chat derender could use a shared `ChatStreamProcessor` (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50550#discussion_r3913908193).

#### Why

After #50550, streaming chat derender (`OnlineDerenderer._derender_chat_stream_parsed`) produces the same `reasoning` / `content` / `tool_calls` deltas that `/v1/chat/completions` streams for the same tokens. To do that it repeats the per choice post parse steps from `OpenAIServingChat.chat_completion_stream_generator`:

- building the parser (`parser_cls(tokenizer, tools, chat_template_kwargs=..., model_config=...)`)
- one `parse_delta` call per chunk
- tracking `tools_streamed`
- rewriting `finish_reason` to `tool_calls` unless a function was named in `tool_choice`
- `maybe_filter_parallel_tool_calls`

The two copies match today. Only code review keeps them that way until the streaming parity tests from #47161 PR3 land and any change to parser handling has to be made in both places. Streaming logprobs on the parsed derender path (after #55029) will add another shared rule drop: logprobs and token IDs when reasoning is hidden (`hide_stream_metadata` in serving).

#### Proposal

Pull a per choice processor out of `chat_completion_stream_generator`. It owns the parser and `tools_streamed` and handles one chunk per step: `parse_delta` → `finish_reason` → parallel tool call filter.

- **Chat serving** uses it for live output. The generator keeps what only serving needs:
  - skipping `None` deltas (unless it's the finish chunk or `return_token_ids` is set)
  - reasoning token counts for usage
  - delta logging
  - error finish reasons
  - `stop_reason` and `token_ids` on the chunk
- **Streaming derender** uses it for both replay and the current chunk. The derenderer keeps what only derender needs:
  - the replay loop over `output_chunk_lens`
  - tool call ID pinning via `last_tool_call_ids`
  - always returning a chunk
  - reading and returning `stream_state`

Responses API streaming stays out. It also calls `parse_delta` but emits a different event shape.

The shared part is thin, so getting the interface right matters more than how much code moves. For chat serving this is a pure refactor with no change to what `/v1/chat/completions` streams. ChatStreamProcessor` is the name from the review and it can change.

#### Sequencing

This should come after #50550 and streaming logprobs (#55029, then the parsed path), so the processor is shaped around both users as they end up. The chat streaming change can then be reviewed on its own. If this lands before the parser cache (#57571), the cache could hold this processor instead of a bare `Parser`.

#### Done when

- [ ] Processor extracted from `chat_completion_stream_generator`. Existing chat streaming and reasoning / tool parser tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] Streaming chat derender moved onto it. `test_derender_stream.py` passes unchanged.
- [ ] The hidden reasoning rule for logprobs and token IDs lives in the processor, so the parsed derender path applies it too.

### Alternatives

- **Do it before #50550 merges as a small PR that #50550 rebases on.** I proposed this in the review (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50550#discussion_r4005719757), then switched to a follow up (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50550#discussion_r4035126957). The code around the shared steps differs enough that it's easier to shape the processor once derender streaming and #55029 are in.
- **Keep the two copies.** Cheapest option. The streaming parity tests from #47161 PR3 would catch drift after the fact but every parser handling change would still have to be made twice.
- **Include the Responses API loop.** It emits a different event shape, so it's a bigger change for little gain.

### Additional context

- RFC #47161 (streaming derender), PR #50550
- #50550 review thread: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50550#discussion_r3913908193
- #55029: streaming logprobs for derender
- Parser cache / server side parser state: #57571

cc @sagearc @chaunceyjiang

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

comments.author: he-yufeng
comments.body:
Independent confirmation plus an edge-case matrix, CPU-only on main @ 4274ae956c with the GLM-4.7 tokenizer.

**Repro confirmed as written.** Your exact script: `content: 'Fetching the page. I will issue a '`, `tool calls: []`. The real call is gone and the finish is a silent stop. The mechanism writeup is accurate: `(TOOL_NAME, TOOL_START)` has no transition, prose accumulates into the phantom's name buffer via the TOOL_NAME content event, and `_accept_tool_name` under `validate_tool_names=True` drops the whole thing at close.

**With the proposed one-transition patch applied** (`(TOOL_NAME, TOOL_START) -> TOOL_NAME` emitting TOOL_CALL_END + TOOL_CALL_START), I ran five probes:

| input shape | result |
|---|---|
| stray tag in prose, then real call (your repro) | real call parsed, correct name + args |
| two consecutive stray tags, then real call | real call parsed, both phantoms dropped |
| literal `<tool_call>` token inside `<arg_value>` | preserved verbatim in the arg string (TOOL_ARGS has no TOOL_START transition, `_emit_for_state` returns it as ARG_VALUE_CHUNK) |
| clean call, no stray | unchanged |
| **lone stray tag, no real call after** | **still silently truncated**: content stops at the stray, 200/stop, nothing emitted |

So the patch fully covers "stray followed by real call" and leaves the lone-stray case as the known residual you flagged for the fuller re-emit fix. I agree with not giving TOOL_ARGS the same transition: quoted markup in values round-trips correctly today, and a recovery there would corrupt legitimate data.

One extra note for the PR: `ling3.py` imports `glm47_moe_config`, so the transition lands there too. Worth a line in the description since the fix's blast radius is wider than the file name suggests.

Suites at the patched head: `tests/parser/engine/test_glm47_moe.py`, `tests/parser/engine/test_parser_engine.py`, `tests/reasoning/test_glm4_moe_reasoning_parser.py` all pass (159), and the full `tests/parser/` tree passes 6312 + 384 subtests with two pre-existing unrelated failures (cohere collection needs `cohere_melody`; `test_auto_with_lark_grammar` fails identically on unpatched main).

You said you're happy to send the PR, and your analysis earned it. If you'd rather hand it off for bandwidth reasons, I have the verified patch and probes sitting in a worktree and can ship it with your issue as the design credit. Either way, glad to review.

items.title: Misc. bug: Vulkan flash_attn.comp writes past the end of Qf in the quantized (MMQ) path
items.author: apollo-2006
items.body_excerpt:
### Name and Version

Built from commit `8a94fc231` (master plus my own merged commit), compiler GNU 16.2.1, Linux x86_64. The version string from this tree reports a build number of 2 because it is a shallow clone, so it is not meaningful. I also confirmed the code below is unchanged on master `c77ae695c93a`.

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

Other (Please specify in the next section)

### Command line

```shell
GGML_VK_DISABLE_COOPMAT=1 VK_LAYER_GPUAV_ENABLE=1 ./build/bin/test-backend-ops -o FLASH_ATTN_EXT
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

This is the Vulkan backend (`ggml-vulkan`), which the dropdown above has no entry for.

In `flash_attn.comp`, the Q load loop checks `is_in_bounds` before writing in the `#ifndef MMQ` branch, but the `#else` (quantized) branch writes with no check. Threads where `r >= Br` therefore write past the end of `Qf`. Nothing crashes and the tests still pass; GPU-AV is what caught it.

The quantized branch does use `is_in_bounds`, but only to zero `vals`; the writes to `Qf[buf_ib]` themselves are unconditional.

Relevant lines (from the loop at `flash_attn.comp` around line 112):

```glsl
const bool is_in_bounds = r < Br && d < HSK / 4 && i * Br + r < N;
#ifndef MMQ
        if (is_in_bounds) {
            Qf[r * qf_stride + d] = ...;                    // guarded
        }
#else
        const uint buf_ib = r * qf_stride + d / 8;
        Qf[buf_ib].qs[buf_iqs] = pack32(i8vec4(vals));      // not guarded
        ...
            Qf[buf_ib].ds = FLOAT_TYPEV2(qd, 0.0f);         // not guarded
```

Seen on `FLASH_ATTN_EXT` with head size 72 and a quantized K/V type, on RADV / RX 9070 XT. `Qf` holds 12 elements there and the writes reach element 31. I only observed head size 72; other head sizes may hit the same path, but I haven't verified them.

### First Bad Commit

Did not bisect

```
n/a
```

items.title: [Bug]: HA snapshot recovery does not update applied sequence metric
items.author: Icedcoco
items.body_excerpt:
### Bug Report

### Summary

When an HA standby starts from a batch OpLog snapshot, the snapshot state and recovery cursor are restored successfully, but the exported `ha_oplog_applied_sequence_id` metric remains at its initial value. This makes the metric disagree with the standby's actual recovery position.

### Reproduction

The issue is reproducible with a snapshot whose recovered sequence is `117` and which has no incremental OpLog entries to apply after the snapshot:

1. Create and publish a valid batch OpLog snapshot covering sequence `117`.
2. Start an HA standby with snapshot bootstrap enabled.
3. Allow snapshot recovery to complete and the standby to enter `WATCHING`.
4. Read the standby metrics and synchronization status.

Observed result:

```text
recovery log:          snapshot/applied = 117
OpLogApplier expected:  118
snapshot applied batch: 51
standby state:          WATCHING
sync status applied:    117
ha_oplog_applied_sequence_id: 0
```

The standby's internal cursor and synchronization status show that sequence `117` has been recovered, while the exported applied-sequence gauge still reports `0`.

### Root cause

`OpLogApplier::Recover(last_applied_sequence_id)` updates only `expected_sequence_id` to `last_applied_sequence_id + 1`. It does not update the HA applied-sequence gauge.

The gauge is currently updated when an individual `ApplyOpLogEntry` succeeds. The snapshot bootstrap path installs the recovered baseline through `HotStandbyService::LoadBatchOpLogSnapshotBaselineLocked` and updates the standby's internal `applied_seq_id_`, but does not update `ha_oplog_applied_sequence_id`. Therefore, a snapshot with an empty incremental tail leaves the exported gauge at its initial value.

### Impact

- Monitoring reports an incorrect applied sequence immediately after snapshot recovery.
- Any alert, readiness check, or recovery validation based on `ha_oplog_applied_sequence_id` or derived lag can report a false failure or an incorrect recovery state.
- Operators cannot distinguish a metric reporting error from an actual OpLog replay failure using the exported metrics alone.

This is an observability and recovery-validation defect. The current evidence does not indicate data loss or incorrect recovered object metadata; the internal recovery cursor is correct.

### Expected behavior

After a successful snapshot recovery, `ha_oplog_applied_sequence_id` must equal the latest sequence represented by the recovered baseline, even when no incremental OpLog entries follow it:

```text
snapshot_applied_sequence = 117
ha_oplog_applied_sequence_id = 117
expected_sequence_id = 118
```

When incremental entries are subsequently applied, the metric must continue advancing to the latest successfully applied sequence.

### Scope of the fix

Synchronize the applied-sequence gauge with the recovered baseline during snapshot/bootstrap installation. Check all recovery paths that establish a baseline, including batch snapshot recovery, ordinary snapshot recovery, and local warm restart, so that the metric does not depend on at least one later OpLog entry being replayed.

Do not change the recovered cursor or treat the metric as the source of truth; the metric should reflect the already recovered cursor.

### Acceptance criteria

Add regression coverage for:

1. Snapshot recovery with no incremental OpLog tail.
2. Snapshot recovery followed by incremental entries.
3. A baseline at sequence `0`.
4. Consistency between the applied sequence, expected sequence, snapshot batch, and lag metrics.

The tests should verify both the internal synchronization status and the exported `ha_oplog_applied_sequence_id` metric.

### Additional context

The metric is defined as the "Latest OpLog sequence ID applied by Standby". A successful snapshot recovery already reports the recovered sequence in recovery logs and synchronization status, so the exported metric should expose the same value rather than remain at its process-start default.


### Before submitting...

- [ ] Ensure you searched for relevant issues and read the [documentation]

comments.author: bryand410
comments.body:
Verified against `main` — @Icedcoco's diagnosis holds at every line it names, and it reaches
further than the report suggests. Four findings, in order of how much they change the fix.

**1. This is not specific to batch snapshots — it hits four start paths.**

`OpLogApplier::Recover` (`mooncake-store/src/ha/oplog/oplog_applier.cpp:153-158`) writes exactly
one thing:

```cpp
void OpLogApplier::Recover(uint64_t last_applied_sequence_id) {
    expected_sequence_id_.store(last_applied_sequence_id + 1);
    LOG(INFO) << "OpLogApplier: recovered from sequence_id=" ...
}
```

The gauge is only advanced from inside `ApplyOpLogEntry` (`oplog_applier.cpp:129-134`), i.e. once
per *replayed entry*. So any path that establishes a baseline without replaying an entry leaves the
exported gauge at its process-start value. There are four, not one:

| Path | Source | Baseline set | Gauge after |
|---|---|---|---|
| Batch OpLog snapshot | `LoadBatchOpLogSnapshotBaselineLocked` (`hot_standby_service.cpp:240-271`, baseline from `:260`) | yes | **stale** |
| Warm restart, recoverable local state | `Recover(local_last_seq_id)` (`hot_standby_service.cpp:218`) | yes | **stale** |
| Ordinary snapshot baseline | `LoadSnapshotBaselineLocked` (`hot_standby_service.cpp:232-238`) | 0 | **never leaves 0** |
| Empty cluster start | same function | 0 | 0 — correct |

Row 3 is the one I'd flag hardest, because it is not a staleness bug but a permanent silence: that
path calls `Recover(0)`, so the gauge stays `0` for the whole life of the process **unless** an
OpLog entry is later replayed. A standby that recovers from an empty baseline and then only serves
reads will export `ha_oplog_applied_sequence_id: 0` forever while its cursor is correct.

Row 2 matters for a different reason: it means this is not a snapshot-bootstrap problem at all. Any
standby process that restarts with local state but no new entries to apply reports `0`.

**2. The two callers of `Recover` do not agree on the contract.** In `LoadSnapshotBaselineLocked`,
`Recover(0)` is followed by `baseline_seq_id` staying `0` — consistent. In
`LoadBatchOpLogSnapshotBaselineLocked`, the baseline is derived *back out* from the applier:

```cpp
baseline_seq_id = oplog_applier_->GetExpectedSequenceId() - 1;   // hot_standby_service.cpp:260
```

That is the applier's state being read as the source of truth for the service's cursor. So the
inconsistency is structural: `Recover` owns `expected_sequence_id_` but not the gauge, while the
caller reconstructs the baseline from the applier. Any fix that only patches the batch-snapshot
path will leave row 2 and row 3 wrong.

**3. The correct value is already computed five lines above, and the gauge ignores it.**

```cpp
batch_snapshot_baseline_ = DurablePrefix{.batch_id = restored->last_applied_batch_id,
                                         .last_seq  = restored->last_applied_seq};   // :261-263
```

So no new plumbing is needed to know the correct number on this path — the value the gauge should
carry is set five lines earlier. Note also that `Recover` sets `expected_sequence_id_` to
`baseline + 1`, and `:260` inverts that back. The two agree today, but they are two independent
expressions of the same quantity, which is worth collapsing while this is being fixed.

**4. On the metric's own tests.** `TestSetOpLogAppliedSequenceId`
(`mooncake-store/tests/ha/standby/ha_metric_manager_test.cpp:154-157`) verifies the setter:

items.title: [Bug]: [Misc] SSD admin CLI tools rebuild full SSH handshake per remote command
items.author: thrower01
items.body_excerpt:
### Bug Report

ontext

Both`python/mooncake/mooncake_ssd_register.py::_execute_ssh_command` and`mooncake_ssd_unregister.py::_execute_ssh_command` open a fresh`paramiko.SSHClient` , run`connect()` , run one command, then call`close()` . No connection reuse.

The register tool calls this function for every SPDK target, and within one target the pattern is:

1. probe`scripts/rpc.py` location (up to 2`test -f` commands)
2. call`nvmf_get_subsystems`
3. for each namespace, call`bdev_get_bdevs`
That is 3 to 5 full SSH handshakes per target — TCP SYN → KEX → userauth → channel open → exec → channel close. Each target pays the handshake multiplier once per discovery run. The unregister tool has the same duplicated code path.

Fix direction

Introduce a process-wide`SSHConnectionPool` in`python/mooncake/_administration.py` keyed by`(ip, port, username, password, key_file)` :

- lazy connect on first`_get_client(key)`
- `get_transport().is_active()` health check before reuse
- single automatic reconnect + retry on`exec_command` failure (handles transient TCP drops)
- `close_all()` /`reset_for_test()` for cleanup
Both admin scripts delegate`_execute_ssh_command()` to the pool. Each SPDK target now shares one SSH handshake across all commands in its discovery flow.

Impact

Reduces per-target handshake count from`O(namespaces + 3)` to`O(1)` ; eliminates repeated KEX CPU work on the remote node; and makes the discovery path resilient to a single transient SSH drop per target. Only affects the two admin CLI tools, which are operator-facing and off the inference / training data path.

Acceptance

- New unit tests covering same-host reuse (1 connect for N commands), cross-host isolation (one connect per distinct host), and reconnect-once after a transient failure.
- Existing`require_paramiko` lazy-import tests keep passing

### Before submitting...

- [x] Ensure you searched for relevant issues and read the [documentation]

items.title: [Perf] DeepSeek-V4 dsv4 prefill on SM120 (4x RTX PRO 6000, TP=4): ~2-7K tok/s vs ~12.5K reported via vLLM/marlin on identical hardware — expected? tuning guidance?
items.author: hassellof
items.body_excerpt:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched existing issues; found SM120 kernel-coverage work (#19637 roadmap, #30272) but nothing on dsv4-backend prefill throughput specifically.
- [x] English.

### Question / observation

DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 on 4× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120, 96 GB, TP=4, PCIe gen5, no NVLink), sglang v0.5.16, `dsv4` attention backend, `flashinfer_mxfp4` MoE, fp8_e4m3 KV: **prefill throughput sits at ~2-7K tok/s**, while a stock **vLLM 0.25.1 recipe on identical hardware reports ~12.5K tok/s prefill at 256K context** (marlin MoE backend, expert parallelism, fp8 KV — https://github.com/hermia-ai/deepseek-v4-flash-sm120-stock-vllm). A 4-6× gap at large context on the same GPUs suggests the SM120 dsv4 prefill path has significant headroom. Is this expected/known, and is there tuning guidance?

### Our measurements (sglang v0.5.16 + the #33407 dispatch fix, DSPARK enabled)

- Aggregate prefill, 9 concurrent ~90K-token prompts: **~5,540 tok/s** (813K prompt tokens / 146.9 s wall; outputs negligible at 61 tokens each)
- Aggregate prefill, 3 concurrent ~650K-token prompts: **~2,805 tok/s** (1.95M / 695.5 s)
- Single ~650K-token prompt: **~2,870 tok/s** (226.4 s to first token)
- Live scheduler logs show per-batch input throughput starting ~6.5K tok/s at low sequence position and declining to ~1.8-2.1K past several hundred K tokens (attention cost growth expected — but the absolute level is the question)
- `--chunked-prefill-size` 4096 vs 8192: statistically identical wall time (146.9 vs 149.0 s on the 9×90K test), so chunking overhead isn't the limiter
- Startup notes `Breakable CUDA graph is incompatible with DeepSeek-V4 (heavy capture-pool memory pressure); disabling prefill CUDA graph` — so DSV4 prefill runs graph-less on this path
- `--max-prefill-tokens` at default 16384; `--disable-flashinfer-autotune` set (SM120 autotune instability, upstream rec)

### Relevant config

```
--tp-size 4 --trust-remote-code
--mem-fraction-static 0.90 --context-length 1048576
--swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1
--max-running-requests 64 --cuda-graph-max-bs 64
--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4
--speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-attention-mode decode
--disable-custom-all-reduce --chunked-prefill-size 4096
--disable-flashinfer-autotune
```

(`--disable-custom-all-reduce` because sgl_kernel custom allreduce fails CUDA-graph capture on our PCIe GPU pairs, #11957 class.)

### Questions

1. Is dsv4-backend prefill on SM120 known to be unoptimized relative to the decode path (which benchmarks well for us — ~1,280 out tok/s at concurrency 64 with DSPARK)?
2. The vLLM recipe uses expert parallelism (`--enable-expert-parallel`) and the marlin MoE backend. Would `--ep-size 4` (or an EP/TP hybrid) be expected to materially improve MoE prefill on PCIe-only SM120 boxes with sglang, and is that combination supported with `flashinfer_mxfp4`?
3. Is the disabled prefill CUDA graph a meaningful contributor at these chunk sizes, or is the gap dominated by MoE GEMM kernel choice on SM120?
4. Any recommended experiments/flags for prefill specifically on this hardware class? Happy to run and report numbers — SM120 hardware is available for validation.

Context: prefill throughput directly bounds a fairness problem we've documented (a single large-context prefill monopolizes chunked-prefill admission for its full duration — several minutes at ~2K tok/s for near-1M prompts — starving concurrent small requests).

items.title: [Bug]  DSV4.1 Flash + DSPARK: CUDA caching allocator exhausts GPU memory under sustained max-batch decode (OOM crash every 15–25 min), KV pool only 29% used
items.author: elain
items.body_excerpt:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

Serving DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with DSPARK speculative decoding on a single 8×B200 node is **stable under short benchmark windows (< 6 min) but crashes on a fixed ~15–25 minute cadence under sustained max-batch decode load**. Every crash has the same signature: all 8 TP ranks fail a 20 MB `expandable_segments` mapping with only 4–19 MB free, then the engine kills its own process tree. Docker restarts it, and it crashes again ~15–25 min later. Over a 2-hour sustained soak: **6 crashes, identical signature**.

Crucially this is **not a KV-cache capacity problem** — at crash time `full token usage: 0.29, swa token usage: 0.16` (KV pool `max_total_num_tokens=25,826,048`, ~71% of KV headroom unused). The PyTorch caching allocator's non-KV memory grows unboundedly under sustained load.

**Allocator failure — all 8 ranks within the same second (two shown):**

[rank0]:[W1010 01:38:17.257967532 CUDACachingAllocator.cpp:508] expandable_segments: memory mapping failed with OOM on device 0 while trying to map 20971520 bytes (free: 4718592, total: 191502876672).
[rank4]:[W1010 01:38:17.258494500 CUDACachingAllocator.cpp:508] expandable_segments: memory mapping failed with OOM on device 4 while trying to map 20971520 bytes (free: 19398656, total: 191502876672).

**Crash handler immediately after:**

[2026-10-10 01:38:23] kill_process_tree called: parent_pid=1, include_parent=True, pid=1
[2026-10-10 01:38:24] No live scheduler processes found; skipping py-spy and CUDA coredump.
[2026-10-10 01:38:24] SIGQUIT received. signum=None, frame=None. It usually means one child failed.

**KV pool NOT exhausted at crash time** (last scheduler lines before death):

Prefill batch, #new-seq: 1, #new-token: 512, #cached-token: 48896, full token usage: 0.29, swa token usage: 0.16, #running-req: 195, #queue-req: 0

**Mitigation experiments we already ran (both failed, so this looks like unbounded growth, not headroom sizing):**

1. Removing `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` → the server crashes even under trivial load (single-digit concurrent probes) right after startup; the fixed-segment allocator is strictly worse here.
2. Lowering `--mem-fraction-static` 0.75 → 0.73 (frees ~3.8 GB/GPU for the allocator) → **crash cadence unchanged** (4 crashes in 5 sustained windows), same signature.

**Related issues checked and ruled out:**
- #36333 (zombie requests after client disconnect): zero occurrences of `"state was deleted in TokenizerManager"` in our logs.
- #37553 (unbounded `custom_mask` via `torch.cat` in EAGLE/DFlash): DSPARK's verify path passes `custom_mask=None` throughout (`dspark_components/dspark_verify.py`), so it does not use that code path.

Secondary observation: before each crash, sustained throughput degrades ~15–20% vs short-window burst and TTFT/ITL p95 drift up, consistent with growing allocator pressure. This makes the current V4.1 preview unfit for sustained saturated serving on our node (`--restart unless-stopped` recovers in ~8 min per crash as a stopgap). Sustained-load stability may be worth adding to the V4.1 roadmap (#42170) — short-window benchmarks cannot catch this bug class. Happy to provide full container logs / dmesg / workload details on request.

### Reproduction

1. Start the server with the command below.
2. Drive **sustained** saturating decode load at high batch — we replay real SWE agent traces at ~192 concurrent sticky sessions with continuous streaming requests (each request carries its full session prefix, up to ~300K tokens). Any sustained max-batch decode workload with DSPARK on should work.
3. Within 15–25 minutes the process dies with the allocator signature above; docker restarts it; it dies again every 15–25 min.
4. Note: 6-minute benchmark windows never trigger it — the failure only appears under sustained load, so a quick `bench_serving` pass will look clean.

Launch command:

```bash
docker run -d --name sglang_standalone --network host --ipc host --gpus all \
  --shm-size 67108864 --restart unless-stopped \
  -v /data/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash:/models:ro \
  -e SGLANG_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE=60 -e PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True \
  lmsysorg/sglang:dev-dsv41 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /models --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --tp 8 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 --trust-remote-code \
  --context-length 1048576 --page-size 64 --mem-fraction-static 0.75 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 32768 --max-prefill-tokens 32768 \
  --max-running-requests 256 --enable-cache-report --enable-metrics \
  --enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay \
  --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-dspark-block-size 5 \
  --log-level info

Startup reference numbers: max_total_num_tokens=25826048, available_gpu_mem≈20.5 GB after init.

### Environment

```markdown
- Hardware: 8 × NVIDIA B200 (192 GB each, SM100), single node, NVLink, host network
- Driver / CUDA: 580.178.04 / CUDA 13.0.3 (in container); torch 2.13.0+cu130; NCCL 2.30.7
- SGLang: `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-dsv41@sha256:4a5d132a06a7` (sglang 0.0.0.dev1+gda64c5cbb) — this is still the newest V4.1 preview digest as of 2026-10-10
- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (476 GB, bundled 3-stage DSPARK draft, `num_nextn_predict_layers=3`)
- Workload: SWE agent-trace session replay — 400 sticky sessions replayed continuously, ~192 concurrent sessions, streaming (`stream=true`, `include_usage`), per-request prompts carry full session history (up to ~300K tokens)
- Quant/KV defaults: KV dtype fp8_e4m3, attention backend dsv

items.title: fp16 and bf16 constants are rounded twice through fp32, 1 ulp off near ties
items.author: shuyilinn
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

fp16 and bf16 constants are rounded twice: from the Python float (a double) to fp32, and then to the 16-bit type. A value just above a 16-bit rounding tie loses the bits that break the tie, and the tie then rounds to even, 1 ulp too low.

```python
import numpy as np
import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl


@triton.jit
def kernel(X, Z, V: tl.constexpr, N: tl.constexpr):
    offs = tl.arange(0, N)
    tl.store(Z + offs, tl.full([N], V, tl.float16))
    tl.store(Z + N + offs, tl.load(X + offs) * V)


v = 1 + 2**-11 + 2**-30  # just above the fp16 tie between 0x3C00 and 0x3C01
z = torch.empty(32, dtype=torch.float16, device="cuda")
kernel[(1, )](torch.ones(16, dtype=torch.float16, device="cuda"), z, V=v, N=16)
print(hex(z.view(torch.uint16)[0].item()), hex(z.view(torch.uint16)[16].item()))
print(hex(np.array([v], np.float16).view(np.uint16)[0]))
```

```
0x3c00 0x3c00
0x3c01
```

Expected `0x3c01` (what numpy gives) for both `tl.full` and the multiplication. bf16 has the same problem, e.g. `1 + 2**-8 + 2**-30` gives `0x3f80` instead of `0x3f81`.

`get_fp16` and `get_bf16` in `python/src/ir.cc` take a C++ `float`, so pybind rounds the double to fp32 before it is converted to the 16-bit type. In the interpreter, `get_bf16` also goes through fp32 (`get_fp16` uses numpy and is correct).

The error is at most 1 ulp, and only for values within an fp32 ulp of a 16-bit tie.

### Environment details

Triton: main @ 41846bc965
GPU: NVIDIA RTX 4090 (sm_89), driver 570 / CUDA 12.8

items.title: `tl.dot` with `input_precision="bf16x3"` or `"bf16x6"` and K=8 returns twice the product
items.author: shuyilinn
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

`tl.dot` on fp32 operands with `input_precision="bf16x3"` or `"bf16x6"` and K=8 returns exactly twice the product. K=8 is accepted for fp32 operands, and `ieee`, `tf32` and `tf32x3` give the right result at K=8.

```python
import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl


@triton.jit
def kernel(A, B, C, K: tl.constexpr, PRECISION: tl.constexpr):
    m = tl.arange(0, 16)
    k = tl.arange(0, K)
    a = tl.load(A + m[:, None] * K + k[None, :])
    b = tl.load(B + k[:, None] * 16 + m[None, :])
    tl.store(C + m[:, None] * 16 + m[None, :], tl.dot(a, b, input_precision=PRECISION))


for precision in ["ieee", "tf32", "tf32x3", "bf16x3", "bf16x6"]:
    for K in (8, 16):
        a = torch.ones(16, K, device="cuda")
        b = torch.ones(K, 16, device="cuda")
        c = torch.empty(16, 16, device="cuda")
        kernel[(1, )](a, b, c, K, precision)
        print(f"{precision:7} K={K:2}: expected {K}, got {c[0, 0].item()}")
```

```
ieee    K= 8: expected 8, got 8.0
ieee    K=16: expected 16, got 16.0
tf32    K= 8: expected 8, got 8.0
tf32    K=16: expected 16, got 16.0
tf32x3  K= 8: expected 8, got 8.0
tf32x3  K=16: expected 16, got 16.0
bf16x3  K= 8: expected 8, got 16.0
bf16x3  K=16: expected 16, got 16.0
bf16x6  K= 8: expected 8, got 16.0
bf16x6  K=16: expected 16, got 16.0
```

The frontend allows K >= 8 for 32-bit operands (`min_dot_size` in `third_party/nvidia/backend/compiler.py`). `F32DotTC` then splits the fp32 dot into bf16 dots with the same K=8, below the K >= 16 that the frontend requires for 16-bit operands. `AccelerateMatmul` relies on that requirement when it picks the MMAv2 operand layout (the comment above the `minBitwidth` computation in `BlockedToMMA` says it assumes K >= 256 / bitwidth), so the bf16 dots with K=8 are lowered as if K were 16. All values are doubled, for every shape and `num_warps` I tried, including batched (3-D) dots.

### Environment details

Triton: main @ 41846bc965
GPU: NVIDIA RTX 4090 (sm_89), driver 570 / CUDA 12.8

items.title: [Bug]: NVFP4 garbage output under torch.compile when per-rank K is not 32-aligned (TP8 on SM120): padded block-scale column reads stale memory; eager/Marlin/aligned-TP correct
items.author: jszzr
items.body_excerpt:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment</summary>

```
vLLM: 0.25.1 (pip install, official wheel)
PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130
flashinfer-python: 0.6.13, flashinfer-cubin: 0.6.13 (no flashinfer-jit-cache installed)
transformers: 5.14.1
OS: Ubuntu 22.04.4, kernel 5.15.0-1069-nvidia, glibc 2.35
Python: 3.10.12
GPU: 8x NVIDIA RTX 6000D (Blackwell workstation, compute capability 12.0 / SM120, ~84 GB each)
Driver: 580.95.05, CUDA 13.0
CPU: 2x AMD EPYC 9575F
```
</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Serving a **ModelOpt NVFP4** checkpoint of a **dense** model (Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct, quantized with nvidia-modelopt 0.45.0, unified HF export — same quant config as `nvidia/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct-NVFP4`: NVFP4, group_size 16, KV cache unquantized, `exclude_modules: [lm_head, model.language_model.embed_tokens, model.visual*]`) on **SM120** produces **completely broken output** with the auto-selected NVFP4 linear kernel, and still-incorrect output with the native CUTLASS kernel. Only Marlin produces correct results.

The checkpoint itself is fine: modelopt's own post-PTQ generation check is coherent, and vLLM with `--linear-backend marlin` is fully correct.

Serve command:

```bash
vllm serve Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct-NVFP4 --quantization modelopt_fp4 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 --max-model-len 16384 --port 8000
    # plus --linear-backend {cutlass|marlin} for the variants below
```

Results per NVFP4 linear kernel (greedy decoding, `temperature=0`):

| `--linear-backend` | Kernel (log line) | `"What is 15 + 27?"` (chat) | `"The capital of France is"` (raw completion) | GSM8K (300, flexible-extract) | MMMU val (300, single-image MC) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| auto | `FlashInferCutlassNvFp4LinearKernel` | `'/Dk'` (byte garbage) | — | **0.0** | **0.07** |
| `cutlass` | `CutlassNvFp4LinearKernel` | fluent but unrelated text (hallucinates an image description) | `'-Zafer Yilmaz\nThe most'` | — | — |
| `marlin` | `MarlinNvFp4LinearKernel` | `'42'` ✅ | `' Paris. The capital of Germany is Berlin'` ✅ | correct (full eval in progress; spot checks all pass) | — |
| (reference) BF16 original model | — | correct | correct | 0.887 | 0.69 |

Two distinct problems:

1. **`FlashInferCutlassNvFp4LinearKernel` is auto-selected on SM120 but is known-broken there.** Its `is_supported()` only checks `has_device_capability(100)`, so SM120 passes. But FlashInfer's `mm_fp4(backend="cutlass")` on SM120 has documented correctness bugs: flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#2577 (still open: cutlass backend returns zeros on RTX PRO 6000), flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#2708 (missing GDC flags → PDL barriers no-op → NaN/garbage tiles under concurrency). SGLang explicitly **gates flashinfer-cutlass FP4 off on SM120** (sgl-project/sglang#18954, fixed by sgl-project/sglang PR #20047 which defaults SM120 to cudnn); vLLM 0.25.1 has no equivalent gate. Suggested fix: exclude SM120 in `FlashInferCutlassNvFp4LinearKernel.is_supported()` (or rank it below the native kernels there).

2. **Native `CutlassNvFp4LinearKernel` (`cutlass_scaled_fp4_mm_sm120a`) also produces incorrect results on SM120** in this setup — output is locally fluent but semantically wrong even for a 5-token greedy completion, which points at numerically corrupted GEMM rather than sampling issues. This one looks like a separate bug in the sm120a path (or its interaction with TP=8).

Happy to run further diagnostics on this machine (8x SM120) — e.g. single-GPU repro with a small NVFP4 model, kernel unit tests, or a patched wheel.

**Workaround for anyone hitting this:** `--linear-backend marlin` gives correct output on SM120 (at reduced prefill throughput vs native FP4).

items.title: [Bug]: Speculative decoding (mtp and dflash) silently disables prefix-cache hits for hybrid GDN models on nightly; worked on v0.24.0
items.author: cgoudie
items.body_excerpt:
(analysis by Fable 5)
### Your current environment

- DGX Spark (GB10, `sm_121`/`sm_121a`, aarch64, 128 GB unified memory), Docker `--network host --gpus all --ipc host`
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` → reports `v0.28.1rc1.dev43+g6f7df92a8`
- Comparison baseline on the same host: `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.24.0`
- Model: `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (hybrid GDN: 48 linear-attention + 16 full-attention layers, built-in MTP head). Also reproduced with `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` + `incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` (rev `dedf8df`).
- `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--max-model-len 65536`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.30`, env `CUTE_DSL_ARCH=sm_121a`

### 🐛 Describe the bug

On the current nightly, enabling **any** speculative decoding method (built-in `mtp` or `dflash`) on a hybrid GDN model silently drops `vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total` to **0** — align-mode prefix caching engages at startup (log: `Mamba cache mode is set to 'align' for Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`) but never hits, and repeated long prompts pay full re-prefill. The identical command minus `--speculative-config` hits normally. No crash, no warning — the caching is just inert, so this is easy to miss in production.

A/B on the same host, same model, same 18,219-token prompt sent twice (`max_tokens=10`):

| nightly config | TTFT req1 → req2 | `prefix_cache_hits_total` delta |
|---|---|---|
| APC only (no spec) | 9.46 s → **0.64 s** | **17,248** |
| APC + `{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}` | 23.6 s → 13.9 s* | **0** |
| APC + `{"method":"dflash", ..., "num_speculative_tokens":7}` | 12.9 s → 12.5 s | **0** |

\* the MTP row also shows a large decode regression on this platform (10.5 tok/s vs 19.7 on v0.24.0 with the same flags — possibly a separate sm_121 issue; noting it for context, not the subject of this report).

**On `v0.24.0`, MTP + align-mode APC coexist correctly** on the same host/model: repeated 9,901-token prompt → 8,000 tokens hit, TTFT 7.27 s → 1.33 s, with `mtp` k=3 active. So spec+APC coexistence for hybrids existed and regressed somewhere between v0.24.0 and the current nightly.

Repro (nightly):

```bash
docker run --rm --init --network host --gpus all --ipc host \
  -v /opt/models:/models -e CUTE_DSL_ARCH=sm_121a \
  vllm/vllm-openai:nightly /models/qwen3.8-27b-nvfp4 \
  --served-model-name bench --port 10099 \
  --max-model-len 65536 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.30 \
  --max-num-seqs 1 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
# send any >3,300-token prompt twice; watch vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total stay 0
# drop --speculative-config and the second send hits ~all full blocks
```

Possibly related but distinct: #53670 (hits occur but recompute per hit), #41884 (DFlash+APC IndexError crash — we see silent zero-hit, not a crash), #26201 (tracking).

Is the suppression intentional (spec-decode + hybrid APC support not yet wired on the new path), or a regression? If intentional, a startup warning like the align-mode one would save users from silently losing their cache. Happy to run further diagnostics on this hardware.

items.title: Multi-NUMA inference - tips and tricks, ideas, commiseration
items.author: DocShotgun
items.body_excerpt:
# Multi-NUMA inference - tips and tricks, ideas, commiseration

Hello folks, I'd like to share my findings messing with all of the different knobs trying to achieve fast local inference on my dual socket homelab server over the past few months. Inviting all multi-NUMA homelab brothers and sisters to chime in with tips, tricks, suggestions, and the joy (pain) of multi-NUMA inference.

First off, I've got a couple of utility scripts to share:

[numactl-bind-socket.sh](https://gist.github.com/DocShotgun/9e7147973fbd358f3685794de38fb90b) - This script binds the following command to a single CPU socket (this is useful for hardware with more than one NUMA node per socket). There are additional options to specify whether to bind all cores (including hyperthreads) or physical cores only, and whether to enable memory interleave. For the purposes of llama.cpp, we generally want to interleave if we are using more than one NUMA node, otherwise it doesn't matter. The syntax is:

`./numactl-bind-socket.sh --socket <id> --mode <physical|all> [--interleave <on|off>] <command> [args...]`

[disable-numa-balancing.sh](https://gist.github.com/DocShotgun/1e4e76b7a67cd44002471022a7561f82) - This script records the current NUMA-balancing state, disables NUMA balancing, then runs any command after it. On quit, it restores the previously recorded NUMA balancing state. The syntax is:

`./disable-numa-balancing.sh <command> [args...]`

---

These are my findings using a dual 8-channel 5th gen Xeon setup with a single RTX Pro 6000 Workstation Edition in CPU+GPU MoE inference:

## Single socket inference

The best settings here seems to be `--no-mmap`, `interleave` + `--numa distribute` (if more than one node per socket). This has fair TG speed and allows for fast op offload to GPU for PP in CPU+GPU setups. Bind to node most proximal to main GPU. NUMA balancing disabled if more than one node per socket.

```
GGML_OP_OFFLOAD_MIN_BATCH=256 \
~/disable-numa-balancing.sh \
~/numactl-bind-socket.sh --socket 0 --mode all --interleave on \
~/llama.cpp/build/bin/llama-server \
-m /mnt/data/models/GGUF/DeepSeek-V3.2-dense-attn-Q8_0-Q4_K-Q4_K-Q5_K/DeepSeek-V3.2-dense-attn-Q8_0-Q4_K-Q4_K-Q5_K-00001-of-00010.gguf \
-c 32768 \
-ngl 999 \
-fa on \
-t 64 \
-b 4096 \
-ub 4096 \
--parallel 1 \
--no-mmap \
-fit off \
--numa distribute \
-ot "blk\.([0-9]|1[0-3])\.=CUDA0,exps=CPU"
```

On single node per socket setups, this would just be isolating to a single node most proximal to the GPU.

Either way we aren't using the hardware to its full potential.

TODO: Difference between `--numa distribute` and `--numa numactl` in this case when binding to 2 nodes?

## Dual socket inference

For models that fit within the RAM of a single socket, using both sockets unfortunately seems to be generally less performant in my experience even though we have twice as many cores and channels available, due to cross-socket access. Open to any new tricks that anyone is aware of!

The best overall setup seems to be `--no-mmap`, `interleave` + `--numa distribute` across as many nodes as are needed to fit the model, with NUMA balancing disabled.

`drop_caches` + `--mmap` + `--numa distribute` trick (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/16000#issuecomment-3293171514): This is interesting. Basically we drop the page cache, then mmap the model and use the warmup pass to "migrate" tensors to the appropriate node based on threads. It's able to achieve higher TG speed than single socket inference, even on models that are small enough to fit on a single socket. However, this seems to *really* hurt PP speeds during op offload to GPU - perhaps the weights are positioned awkwardly in memory so that it's less efficient to copy to GPU for op offload?

TODO: Second socket as RPC device? Curious if anyone has experience with this.

## Repack buffers (i.e. AMX)

I haven't been able to find a good use for these in the CPU+GPU setting, but I suspect they are useful for CPU only inference. With `--no-host`, we can enable repack buffers to use in conjunction with GPU. However, this disables disaggregated op offload PP since there are no host buffers. Generally, this doesn't seem to be worthwhile to do because GPU PP is still faster than repack CPU PP.

## Suggestions

Any observations and tips from your experience welcome. What future NUMA-specific optimizations would you like to see in llama.cpp?

items.title: Eval bug: draft-mtp draft model fails to load with -ngl (vector::_M_range_check 1 >= 1); explicit -ts fixes it — likely NaN split when device reports 0 free
items.author: wyegelwel
items.body_excerpt:
### Summary

With the main model offloaded to the GPU (`-ngl 99`), loading an MTP draft via `--spec-type draft-mtp --model-draft <mtp.gguf>` fails inside `llama_model_load` for the draft with:

```
E llama_model_load: error loading model: vector::_M_range_check: __n (which is 1) >= this->size() (which is 1)
E common_speculative_init_result: failed to load draft model, '.../mtp-Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_0.gguf'
```

Passing an explicit `-ts 1` makes it load and work (single GPU). So the failure is in the *default* tensor-split path.

### Environment

- llama.cpp master `81aeaeb74` (2026-09-17; also reproduced on `37b53fd45`, 2026-09-16), CUDA 12.2 build, `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=86`
- RTX 3080 Laptop 16 GB, driver 596.52, **WSL2** (Ubuntu 22.04)
- Main model: `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF` UD-IQ4_XS and UD-Q3_K_XL (both reproduce)
- Draft: `ggml-org/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF` `mtp-Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_0.gguf` **and** `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF` `MTP/mtp-Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_0.gguf` (both reproduce; both sha256-verified)

### Repro

```
llama-server -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q3_K_XL.gguf -ngl 99 --spec-type draft-mtp --model-draft mtp-Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_0.gguf
```

### What does / doesn't change it

| variant | result |
|---|---|
| as above | **fails** (range_check) |
| `-ngld 0` (draft on CPU) | loads, runs (no speedup, as expected) |
| `-ngld 1`, `-ngld 2` | fails |
| `-devd CUDA0`, `-dev CUDA0 -devd CUDA0` | fails |
| `--fit off` | fails |
| no `-ngl` at all (main on CPU) | loads |
| **`-ts 1`** (explicit single-device split) | **loads; 1.9× decode with 71–82% acceptance** |
| draft file loaded *alone* as the main model with `-ngl 99` | loads fine |

The throw happens right after `load_tensors: loading model tensors...` for the draft, before any tensor is created — i.e. in the device/layer assignment.

### Likely cause (not confirmed with a debugger — none available on this box)

In `llama_model::load_tensors`, when `tensor_split` is all-zero the split is built from `ggml_backend_dev_memory` *free* bytes and then normalized by their sum. When the main model has already filled the card, the device can report **free = 0 with total > 0** (WSL's CUDA memory reporting does this), so `split_sum == 0`, `splits[0] = 0/0 = NaN`, and

```cpp
const int layer_gpu = std::upper_bound(splits.begin(), splits.begin() + n_devices(), float(il - i_gpu_start)/act_gpu_layers) - splits.begin();
auto * dev = devices.at(layer_gpu).dev;
```

`upper_bound` against NaN returns `end`, giving `layer_gpu == n_devices()` → `devices.at(1)` on a 1-device vector → exactly `__n (1) >= size (1)`. The existing `free == 0 && total == 0` fallback doesn't cover the free-only-zero case. An explicit `-ts` skips the free-memory branch, which is why it fixes it; the draft alone works because the GPU is empty at that point.

A guard like "if `split_sum == 0`, fall back to equal splits" (or treating `free == 0` like the existing `free == 0 && total == 0` case) would avoid it.

### Workaround for others hitting this

Add `-ts 1` (single GPU) or an explicit per-device split.
