items.title: [Performance] Dot-operand conversion hoisting replicates integer metadata packing
items.author: IlyasMoutawwakil
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the issue

While optimizing a BF16 × INT4 weight-only GEMM, I found that dot-operand layout-conversion hoisting moves compact integer metadata packing into a layout that replicates the arithmetic. Keeping the packing before the transfer is faster in this workload, provided the transfer is also scheduled before the large MMA operand loads.

This is a performance issue; outputs are correct. The measured gain from an experimental compiler change is small (~1.4%), but the layout/scheduling interaction seemed worth reporting.

### Standalone pass reproducer

Save the following as `repro.py` and run `python repro.py`. It only needs Triton; no Torch, GPU, project package, or checkpoint is needed. This reproduces the pass transformation, **not the full GEMM timing**. Both halves of the packed metadata are consumed and the result feeds the dot operand.

```python
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
import triton
from triton._C.libtriton import ir, passes, nvidia

CASE = r"""
// RUN: triton-opt %s -tritongpu-remove-layout-conversions -cse
#load = #ttg.blocked<{sizePerThread = [1, 2], threadsPerWarp = [16, 2], warpsPerCTA = [2, 1], order = [1, 0]}>
#expanded = #ttg.linear<{register = [[0, 0, 1], [0, 0, 2], [0, 0, 4], [8, 0, 0], [0, 0, 32], [0, 0, 64], [0, 1, 0], [0, 2, 0]], lane = [[0, 0, 8], [0, 0, 16], [1, 0, 0], [2, 0, 0], [4, 0, 0]], warp = [[16, 0, 0]], block = []}>
#meta = #ttg.slice<{dim = 2, parent = #expanded}>
#mma = #ttg.nvidia_mma<{versionMajor = 2, versionMinor = 0, warpsPerCTA = [2, 1], instrShape = [16, 8]}>
#dot0 = #ttg.dot_op<{opIdx = 0, parent = #mma, kWidth = 8}>
#dot1 = #ttg.dot_op<{opIdx = 1, parent = #mma, kWidth = 8}>
module attributes {"ttg.num-ctas" = 1 : i32, "ttg.num-warps" = 2 : i32, "ttg.threads-per-warp" = 32 : i32} {
  tt.func @replicated_integer_metadata(%zp: tensor<32x4x!tt.ptr<i8>, #load>, %a: tensor<512x2xbf16, #dot1>, %weights: tensor<32x4xi32, #meta>, %acc: tensor<32x2xf32, #mma>) -> tensor<32x2xf32, #mma> {
    %magic = arith.constant dense<49920> : tensor<32x4xi32, #load>
    %dup = arith.constant dense<65537> : tensor<32x4xi32, #load>
    %z = tt.load %zp : tensor<32x4x!tt.ptr<i8>, #load>
    %wide = arith.extui %z : tensor<32x4xi8, #load> to tensor<32x4xi32, #load>
    %lifted = arith.ori %wide, %magic : tensor<32x4xi32, #load>
    %packed = arith.muli %lifted, %dup : tensor<32x4xi32, #load>
    %converted = ttg.convert_layout %packed : tensor<32x4xi32, #load> -> tensor<32x4xi32, #meta>
    %pairs = tt.elementwise_inline_asm "add.rn.bf16x2 $0, $1, $2;" {constraints = "=r,r,r", packed_element = 1 : i32, pure = true} %weights, %converted : tensor<32x4xi32, #meta>, tensor<32x4xi32, #meta> -> tensor<32x4xi32, #meta>
    %shift = arith.constant dense<16> : tensor<32x4xi32, #meta>
    %hi32 = arith.shrui %pairs, %shift : tensor<32x4xi32, #meta>
    %hi16 = arith.trunci %hi32 : tensor<32x4xi32, #meta> to tensor<32x4xi16, #meta>
    %hibf = tt.bitcast %hi16 : tensor<32x4xi16, #meta> -> tensor<32x4xbf16, #meta>
    %lo = arith.trunci %pairs : tensor<32x4xi32, #meta> to tensor<32x4xi16, #meta>
    %bf = tt.bitcast %lo : tensor<32x4xi16, #meta> -> tensor<32x4xbf16, #meta>
    %sum = arith.addf %bf, %hibf : tensor<32x4xbf16, #meta>
    %ex = tt.expand_dims %sum {axis = 2 : i32} : tensor<32x4xbf16, #meta> -> tensor<32x4x1xbf16, #expanded>
    %bc = tt.broadcast %ex : tensor<32x4x1xbf16, #expanded> -> tensor<32x4x128xbf16, #expanded>
    %lhs = tt.reshape %bc : tensor<32x4x128xbf16, #expanded> -> tensor<32x512xbf16, #dot0>
    %out = tt.dot %lhs, %a, %acc, inputPrecision = tf32 : tensor<32x512xbf16, #dot0> * tensor<512x2xbf16, #dot1> -> tensor<32x2xf32, #mma>
    tt.return %out : tensor<32x2xf32, #mma>
  }
}
"""

print("Triton:", triton.__version__)
ctx = ir.context()
ir.load_dialects(ctx)
nvidia.load_dialects(ctx)
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    source = Path(directory) / "repro.mlir"
    source.write_text(CASE)
    module = ir.parse_mlir_module(str(source), ctx)
    pm = ir.pass_manager(ctx)
    passes.ttgpuir.add_remove_layout_conversions(pm)
    passes.common.add_cse(pm)
    pm.run(module, "repro")
    print(module)
```

Alternatively, the `CASE` string can be saved as `repro.mlir` and run with:

```sh
triton-opt repro.mlir -tritongpu-remove-layout-conversions -cse
```

On stock v3.8.0, the relevant output order is:

```text
load i8 in producer layout
convert_layout i8 to replicated layout
extui
ori
muli
... packed BF16 arithmetic and dot ...
```

The producer has two unique metadata elements per thread; the destination slice layout has eight. The packing arithmetic therefore runs on four times as many elements per thread. The input IR already places the i32 packing before its conversion, but the pass hoists the conversion above it.

Could `hoistConvertDotOperand` account for this replication cost while preserving weight-load pipelining? The ordinary rematerialization path already has `getCostFactor`/`isRematBeneficial`, whereas this hoisting path walks through pure elementwise operations to the loads without that profitability check:

- [v3.8.0 implementation](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/c01b6774b1865984607d89d89d3a10833de92037/lib/Dialect/TritonGPU/Transforms/RemoveLayoutConversions.cpp#L1237)
- [Current main implementation inspected](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/2122e24efc1886bfa36337c1f5b07c47d827b1d4/lib/Dialect/TritonGPU/Transforms/RemoveLayoutConversions.cpp#L1227)

### Full-workload observations

The originating workload is a dense weight-only GEMM: M=2, N=12288, K=4096; BF16 activations/scales; asymmetric INT4 weights; UINT8 zero points; group size 128. Frozen configuration: BM2/BN32/BK512, pointer loads, transposed operand orientation, two warps, three stages, split-K 1. It uses packed BF16 dequantization with the scale-dtype rounding preserved.

Seven alternating CUDA-graph measurements of the same public wrapper and identical weights/configuration:

| | Stock v3.8.0 | Experimental compiler

items.title: [ModelClaim] Add a Grafana dashboard for high-density runtime pools
items.author: Jeffwan
items.body_excerpt:
### Feature Description and Motivation

ModelClaim needs a dedicated Grafana dashboard for operating experimental high-density GPU runtime pools. Existing dashboards do not present ModelClaim lifecycle, per-engine runtime health, or kvcached allocation in one view.

This issue is intentionally separate from adding missing Prometheus metrics. The dashboard should use the metrics available on the target branch and may be completed after the operational-metrics issue lands.

### Use Case

An operator should be able to open one dashboard and answer:

- Which ModelClaims are active, activating, sleeping, or failed?
- Which pool or Pod hosts each model and how dense is the pool?
- Are engines restarting or exhausting restart budgets?
- How are KV capacity and current KV use distributed among co-resident models?
- Is the pool policy applying changes, skipping unsafe plans, or failing actions?
- How much HBM headroom remains and which engines have the largest observed peak?

### Proposed Solution

Add a dashboard JSON under `observability/grafana/` with:

- namespace, pool, Pod, and model variables;
- ModelClaim desired/ready and lifecycle overview;
- resident model count per runtime Pod;
- per-model KV used, KV limit/capacity, and HBM peak panels;
- engine restart/failure and agent re-adoption panels;
- policy action/skip/failure panels;
- sleep/wake activity and no-ready duration panels;
- links or annotations that make Kubernetes Events/log investigation straightforward.

Follow the repository's existing dashboard conventions. Avoid panels that depend on free-form/high-cardinality labels. Include a short README section describing required metrics and how to import or provision the dashboard.

### Acceptance Criteria

- Dashboard JSON is checked in under `observability/grafana/` and is valid JSON.
- Empty/no-data states render cleanly.
- Variables allow a user to narrow from namespace/pool to Pod/model.
- Panels do not use metrics outside the documented ModelClaim metric contract.
- The dashboard works with multiple warm pools and multiple co-resident models.

items.title: Assertion in TritonAMDGPUCanonicalizePointers: "expected then yield to report fat ptr indices" on a pointer select inside a runtime scf.if
items.author: O1iveira7
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

Compiling a legal Triton kernel fails with a C++ assertion in the AMD `TritonAMDGPUCanonicalizePointers` pass. The kernel merges two pointer bases with `tl.where` under a tensor condition inside a runtime `if`; the pass then hits a mixed representation between the two `scf.if` arms and aborts compilation.


**Error log**
```
CanonicalizePointers.cpp:1445: ... ConvertSCFIfOp::matchAndRewrite_(scf::IfOp, OneToNOpAdaptor, ...):
Assertion ifOp.thenYield()->hasAttr(kSCFIfOpYieldFatPtrOffsets) &&
          "expected then yield to report fat ptr indices" failed.
note: Pipeline failed while executing [TritonAMDGPUCanonicalizePointers` on 'tt.func' operation: @kernel]
RuntimeError: PassManager::run failed

Failure is in `make_ttgir` (MLIR), before LLVM codegen; exit code 1.
```

The generated TTGIR is:

```
%5 = scf.if %4 -> (tensor<2x!tt.ptr<f32>>) {
  %11 = tt.addptr %10, %0          // base = splat(arg1)
  %12 = arith.select %9, %11, %2   // tensor condition, different bases
  scf.yield %12
} else {
  scf.yield %2                     // base = splat(arg2)
}
%8 = tt.load %5
```
TritonAMDGPUCanonicalizePointers is a 1:N conversion to fat pointers (scalar base, tensor offset). scf.if is only rewritten after both scf.yields are rewritten (tracked via internal then/else-rewritten attributes). ConvertSCFYieldOp sets kSCFIfOpYieldFatPtrOffsets on a yield only when one of its remapped operands is a 2-element fat pointer, while ConvertSCFIfOp unconditionally asserts that the then-yield has that attribute.

Here ConvertArithSelectOp takes its special case for a tensor condition with differing scalar bases and materializes both arms into full tensor pointers instead of a (base, offset) pair. So the then-yield carries a single materialized pointer and gets no fat-pointer index attribute, while the else-yield (a plain tt.addptr) converts to a fat pointer pair and does get the attribute. Both yields are marked rewritten, the scf.if becomes illegal, ConvertSCFIfOp fires, and the assertion fails on the inconsistent arms.

**Reproducer**
```
import os

import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl


@triton.jit
def kernel(sw, a_ptr, b_ptr, BLOCK: tl.constexpr):
    offs = tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
    p = b_ptr + offs
    if tl.load(sw) == 0:
        p = tl.where(offs >= 0, a_ptr + offs, b_ptr + offs)
    tl.store(a_ptr + offs, tl.load(p))


def _main() -> None:
    device = "cuda"
    N = 2
    a = torch.randn(N, device=device)
    b = torch.randn(N, device=device)
    sw = torch.tensor([0], dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
    print(f"REPRO_START N={N} buffer_ops={os.environ.get('AMDGCN_USE_BUFFER_OPS', 'default')}", flush=True)
    kernel[(1,)](sw, a, b, BLOCK=N, num_warps=1)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    print("REPRO_DONE (no crash)", flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    _main()
```

### Environment details

- AMD Instinct MI308X (gfx942), ROCm 7.2.3
- triton-rocm 3.8.0, torch 2.14.0+rocm7.2, Python 3.12.13

comments.author: he-yufeng
comments.body:
Picking this up; the earlier attempt #12182 is closed unmerged and the assert is still in place on current main (2a514c0f).

The mechanism in the report checks out. The trigger is the tensor-condition case of ConvertArithSelectOp: with different scalar bases it materializes both arms into full tensor pointers, so the then yield carries one plain pointer and ConvertSCFYieldOp records no fat-ptr offsets for it, while the else yield still carries a (base, offset) pair and does get the attribute. Once both yields are marked rewritten, ConvertSCFIfOp fires and asserts on the asymmetry. Reproduced locally with triton-opt on an asserts-enabled build, same assert as the report (CanonicalizePointers.cpp:1450).

That asymmetric shape is legal output of the select conversion, and downstream consumers already accept a materialized pointer (MaterializeFatPointer passes through any pointer operand that does not arrive as a pair), so the natural place for the fix is the scf.if boundary: for each result where the two yields disagree on the representation, materialize the (base, offset) side into a tensor pointer before rebuilding the op. Results that stay fat on both sides keep the pair form and the existing attribute propagation. The same hole exists when both arms materialize (neither yield reports offsets and the old code asserts on the then yield all the same); the fix covers that shape too.

PR coming with lit coverage for both. No AMD hardware here, so verification is at the MLIR level only.

items.title: Feature Request: Graceful reasoning budget termination. Avoid mid-sentence cutoff.
items.author: CleStil
items.body_excerpt:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well.
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description

PR #20297 (merged ~2025-03-11) added `--reasoning-budget-message`, which injects
a string at the hard token cutoff to signal the model to wrap up. The injection
still happens at exactly token N with zero warning. The model gets no time to
finish its current thought before the `</think>` boundary.

Graceful termination before the cutoff is expected to improve reasoning
performance. See Motivation and Possible Implementation for details.


### Motivation

Raw truncation of the thinking trace measurably reduces answer quality compared
to graceful termination. Muennighoff et al. (s1: Simple test-time scaling,
arXiv:2501.19393) showed that appending an end-of-thinking delimiter with
"Final Answer:" before the hard cut outperforms naïve truncation. This was
confirmed by follow-up work (arXiv:2505.05315), which states directly that
"the S1 approach performs better than directly truncating the full reasoning
trajectory, underscoring the importance of preserving the solution segment."

The current --reasoning-budget-message implementation injects a wrap-up message
at exactly token N, leaving the model zero tokens to actually act on it. This is
functionally equivalent to truncation with a cosmetic suffix — the model cannot
produce a meaningful conclusion within 0 remaining tokens.

### Possible Implementation

Three approaches in increasing complexity:

Option A — message offset
Inject the budget message at `budget - offset` instead of `budget`, giving the
model `offset` tokens to act on the wrap-up signal. The s1 paper
(https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.19393) shows this outperforms raw truncation.
Change in the COUNTING state of reasoning-budget.cpp:

    if (ctx->remaining <= ctx->warn_offset)  // was: <= 0

Files: reasoning-budget.cpp, reasoning-budget.h, common.h, arg.cpp,
sampling.cpp. Default 0 preserves current behavior.

Option B — separate budgeting
Split total budget into thinking (t) and conclusion (s) phases, t + s = budget.
Force `</think>` at token t, leave s tokens for a conclusion before the answer.
Follow-up work on s1 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.05315) shows this outperforms
the basic offset approach. Would add a second parameter, e.g.
--reasoning-budget-conclusion M.

Option C — logit biasing toward `</think>`
Ramp up the logit weight of `</think>` as the budget runs low, then force it at
the hard limit. No dependency on an injected phrase, model-agnostic. NVIDIA NIM
uses this approach with a 10% extension window for sentence completion. More
invasive (sampler changes) but cleanest long-term.

Options A and B build on the existing message injection architecture. Option C
is a parallel approach that could coexist with either.

Happy to test on ROCm/gfx1100 (Qwen3.5-27B) and contribute a draft of Option A
or B if there is interest.

items.title: [Feature] kv-shard: Pass Q instead of KV for short prefills with long cached prefixes
items.author: Shunkangz
items.body_excerpt:
### Checklist

- [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Motivation

## Background

With `--enable-kv-cache-sharding`, each CP rank stores \(1/N\) of every cached prefix. Today, extend batches are zigzag-split across all ranks, and every request’s prefix KV is all-gathered to every rank one layer ahead.

For agentic and multi-turn workloads, a short prefill often extends a long cached prefix, so prefix KV dominates communication. DCP avoids this for decode by passing Q instead of KV, but directly applying it to prefill would replicate new-token computation across ranks.

## Overall Design

Use **per-request placement**: each request has one home CP rank that computes all its new tokens. Choose the communication policy per request based on \(P/T\):

- Pass-KV for short prefixes: the home fetches only its requests’ prefix stripes via all-to-all.
- Pass-Q for long prefixes: all-gather Q, attend over each rank’s local prefix stripes, and return partial outputs and LSE to the home for merging with its causal new-token attention.

Overlap both pass-Q collectives with the home’s local attention and use copy-engine transfers for large messages. In the 8× B200 per-layer harness, exposed communication is 0.1–1.2% of layer time at 128K–256K prefixes; choosing pass-Q when \(P/T > 128\) is within 1.9% of the best measured split on average.

## PR Stack

The following PRs will be released soon.

### 1/5 — Enable FA4 for GQA KV Sharding and Fix Sharded KV Writes

- Enable FA4 for GQA KV sharding on Blackwell.
- Fix a silent wrong-logits bug where fused RoPE + KV writes bypass the sharded pool on short extends, affecting both FA3 and FA4.
- Validation: sharded and unsharded outputs are bit-exact at CP4.

### 2/5 — Add Symmetric-Memory Transports for Pass-Q Attention

- Add `PassQCommunicator` with variable-size Q all-gather, partial O + LSE all-to-all, and LSE merging.
- Support Triton SM-push and copy-engine transports using Torch symmetric memory.
- Add multi-GPU tests.

### 3/5 — Add Per-Request CP Placement for Prefill

- Assign whole requests to CP ranks when the batch can be balanced, using one FA call per rank.
- Fetch only each rank’s own requests’ prefix stripes via all-to-all instead of all-gathering every prefix.
- Validation: sharded and unsharded outputs are bit-exact at CP4 with B=4.
- Reduce latency versus zigzag placement by 8 ms unsharded and 5 ms sharded at 32K/64K.

### 4/5 — Pass Q Instead of KV for Long-Prefix Requests

- Add `--kv-shard-pass-q-ratio` for per-request P/T policy selection.
- Add pass-Q-aware placement, including B < N, and pool stripe tables.
- Implement Q all-gather, local prefix-stripe attention, partial O + LSE all-to-all, and merging.
- Start with a serial schedule.

### 5/5 — Overlap Pass-Q Communication with Local Attention

- Run communication on a side stream.
- Split the home rank’s local attention across both collectives to **overlap** communication and computation.
- Select the transport by message size.
- Run end-to-end A/B validation at CP8.

### Related resources

_No response_

items.title: Use atomic_cas inside a loop
items.author: giorgio-arena
items.body_excerpt:
Hi, I'm experimenting with a simple kernel that reduces a rank-3 tensor on its last dimension. The kernel uses atomics to sum across one tensor row (I know it's not efficient, this is just a simple reproducer). I'm using two versions of the atomics, the first using atomic_add, and the second using the lock-like mechanism with atomic_cas and atomic_xchg.

```
@triton.jit
def _sum_kernel(X, Locks, O, width: tl.constexpr, use_atomic_add: tl.constexpr):
  in_off = tl.program_id(0) * width
  out_off = tl.program_id(0)

  for w in range(0, width):
    x = tl.load(X + in_off + w)
    if use_atomic_add:
      tl.atomic_add(O + out_off, x)
    else:
      while tl.atomic_cas(Locks + out_off, 0, 1) == 1:
        pass
      tl.store(O + out_off, tl.load(O + out_off) + x)
      tl.atomic_xchg(Locks + out_off, 0)


def _sum_fn(a, use_atomic_add):
  b, h, w = a.shape
  locks = torch.zeros([b, h], dtype=torch.int32, device='cuda')
  out = torch.zeros([b, h], dtype=a.dtype, device='cuda')
  _sum_kernel[(b * h,)](a, locks, out, width=w, use_atomic_add=use_atomic_add)
  return out

if __name__ == "__main__":
  x = torch.empty((8, 64, 128), dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda").normal_()
  ref = torch.sum(x, axis=-1)
  rtol = 1e-03

  print(torch.allclose(ref, _sum_fn(x, True), rtol=rtol))
  print(torch.allclose(ref, _sum_fn(x, False), rtol=rtol))
```

Unfortunately for the second version I get
```

  File "/usr/local/home/giorgio/triton/python/triton/compiler.py", line 741, in visit_For
    assert for_op_region.size() == 1, "We use SCF, so the loop body should only have one block"
AssertionError: We use SCF, so the loop body should only have one block
```

Any help would be appreciated, thanks.

items.title: [Interpreter] bfloat16 arithmetic returns wrong values (computed on raw bits)
items.author: roy6n23
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

Under `TRITON_INTERPRET=1`, bfloat16 kernels silently produce wrong results. The interpreter stores bf16 tensors as raw `uint16` bits, and only the bf16 <-> fp32/fp16 casts decode them. Everything else (arithmetic, comparisons, `tl.dot`, `tl.sum`/`tl.cumsum`, `tl.maximum`) runs numpy on the integer bit patterns.

I hit this while testing a FlashAttention-2 forward kernel under the interpreter: every bf16 case was off by about 8e8 while fp16 matched, and the same kernel passes on an H100.

Repro:

```python
import os

os.environ["TRITON_INTERPRET"] = "1"

import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl


@triton.jit
def kernel(x_ptr, y_ptr, add_ptr, dot_ptr, N: tl.constexpr):
    offs = tl.arange(0, N)[:, None] * N + tl.arange(0, N)[None, :]
    x = tl.load(x_ptr + offs)
    y = tl.load(y_ptr + offs)
    tl.store(add_ptr + offs, x + y)
    tl.store(dot_ptr + offs, tl.dot(x, y))


torch.manual_seed(0)
for dtype in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16):
    x, y = torch.randn(16, 16, dtype=dtype), torch.randn(16, 16, dtype=dtype)
    add, dot = torch.empty_like(x), torch.empty(16, 16)
    kernel[(1, )](x, y, add, dot, N=16)
    print(f"{dtype}: max |add - ref| = {(add.float() - (x + y).float()).abs().max().item():.3g}, "
          f"max |dot - ref| = {(dot - x.float() @ y.float()).abs().max().item():.3g}")
```

Output on main (596bd30):

```
torch.float16: max |add - ref| = 0, max |dot - ref| = 0
torch.bfloat16: max |add - ref| = nan, max |dot - ref| = 2.44e+10
```

Two related cast issues: fp32 -> bf16 truncates instead of rounding to nearest even (the default in `semantic.cast`), and int -> bf16 writes the integer as bits, e.g. `(1 < 2).to(tl.bfloat16)` gives 9.2e-41.

The test suite doesn't catch this because bf16 is skipped under the interpreter (`check_type_supported`, plus skips in `test_dot`, `test_scaled_dot` and `test_dot_multidim`). With those skips removed, 527 of the 1,338 bf16 interpreter tests fail on main.

I have a patch that keeps bf16 stored as bits but decodes to fp32 for computation and rounds results back to bf16 with round-to-nearest-even, the same fp32 intermediate the interpreter already uses for bf16 <-> fp16 casts (#11699). With it the skips can be removed: 1,836 previously skipped interpreter tests pass with no regressions. Only bf16 atomics would keep a skip, since they already raise "Unsupported data type". Would a PR along these lines be welcome?

### Environment details

Triton: main @ 596bd30 (3.9.0+git596bd304), built from source; also reproduces with the 3.8.0 wheel
OS: macOS 15.7 arm64, CPU only with TRITON_INTERPRET=1 (3.8.0 also checked on Linux aarch64)
GPU: none (interpreter)
Python 3.12.12, numpy 2.5.3, torch 2.14.1 (CPU)

items.title: [RFC][Plugin] Add MLIR Dialect Whitelist for Preserving TypeIDs and Generic Plugin Module Extension
items.author: hongziqi
items.body_excerpt:
## Abstract

The upstream Triton plugin system only supports table-driven registration of Passes, Dialects, and OpInfo. **It cannot let a plugin inject a custom IR Builder subclass.** At the same time, `libtriton.so` built with `--as-needed` drops TypeIDs of dialects such as Linalg and Tensor.
Triton-Ascend ships as the out-of-tree plugin `libtriton_ascend.so` and shares one MLIRContext / PassManager with the host. In that setup, Pass execution breaks and IR construction fails.

This proposal has two parts:

1. Bump the plugin ABI to v3. Add a host-side module extension callback, `HostExtendCallback`, and a top-level Python API, `ir.extend_module_with`. Build nanobind as its own shared library.
2. Add a dialect whitelist so the listed dialect TypeIDs stay in `libtriton.so` at link time.

After the change, an out-of-tree plugin can attach a custom IR Builder, extend the Python IR with a submodule, and reuse the host MLIR context and Pass pipeline.

## 1. Background

Triton-Ascend uses the **out-of-tree plugin** `libtriton_ascend.so`. It shares the upstream Triton MLIRContext and PassManager, reuses the existing Dialects, Passes, and OpInfo, and does not fork the main repository.

Two gaps show up when this is wired up: a custom IR Builder cannot be injected, and MLIR dialect TypeIDs are missing between the host and the plugin.

### 1.1 GAP-P2: Missing Linalg/Tensor TypeIDs

Upstream `libtriton.so` is built with `--as-needed` by default. If a symbol in a static library is not referenced directly by a host translation unit, the linker drops that archive member. TypeIDs for Linalg, Tensor, and the Complex and Bufferization dialects that Ascend lowering depends on are stripped. When the plugin and the host share one MLIRContext, the required MLIR symbols are missing and Pass execution fails.

### 1.2 GAP-P1: The current plugin mechanism cannot support a custom IR Builder subclass

What the existing plugin extension APIs can and cannot do:

| API | Capability | Typical use | Limit for Ascend |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `passes.plugin.extend_with` | Register Passes and expose `add_*` callbacks | Add an MLIR Pass | Sufficient for Passes |
| `ir.extend_dialects_with` | Register a new Dialect | Add a standalone dialect | Sufficient for Dialect registration |
| `ir.builder.extend_with` (OpInfo table) | Attach op factories on the upstream `ir.builder`. C++ ABI is `void (*)(TritonOpBuilder&, vector<Value>&)`. Host Python wraps it as `create_*(list[Value]) → Value` | Add a simple Op whose arguments are a fixed list of Values | **Not sufficient** |

`ir.builder.extend_with` only supports flat op factory functions. **It does not support a Builder subclass, kwargs, or affine expressions.**
Ascend's `AscendNPUIROpBuilder` subclasses `TritonOpBuilder`, and the IR construction lives in `ascend_ir.cc`. The OpInfo table can only append `create_*` factories. **It cannot replace the Builder type, and it cannot add a Python IR submodule.**

The missing piece is a **host IR module extension hook (HostExtend)** so a plugin can initialize its own IR module inside the host process.

## 2. Design

Each gap maps to an upstream change and a plugin-side hookup:

| Gap | Upstream change | Ascend plugin hookup |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Linalg / Tensor TypeIDs are not visible** | Add a dialect TypeID whitelist, `python/src/plugin_ext_dialects.whitelist`. CMake reads it and generates `plugin_ext_dialects.gen.cc`, which takes a strong reference with `TypeID::get`. On GNU ld, `--whole-archive` pulls the corresponding dialect static libraries into `libtriton.so`. The initial list is Linalg, Tensor, Complex, and Bufferization. | The plugin reuses the whitelisted dialect TypeIDs exported by the host. TypeIDs of plugin-defined dialects stay inside the plugin `.so`. |
| **`ir.builder` factories are not expressive enough** | Add `HostExtensionArgs` and `HostExtendCallback`. Append an `extend` field at the end of `PluginInfo`, read only when `apiVersion >= 3`. Add the top-level Python API `ir.extend_module_with`. When `TRITON_EXT_ENABLED=1`, build nanobind as a separate `libnanobind.so`. | The plugin sets `PluginInfo.extend = ascendExtendHost`. The callback registers a nanobind submodule and exposes `ir._ascend` and `AscendNPUIROpBuilder`. The plugin is built with `NB_SHARED` and links the host `libnanobind.so`. |

Benefits:

- **IR**: An out-of-tree plugin can inject a Builder subclass, with kwargs, affine expressions, and custom op wrappers, instead of being limited to the fixed OpInfo signature `create_*(list[Value])`.
- **ABI**: The v3 `extend` field is appended at the end of `PluginInfo`. The host reads it only when `apiVersion >= 3`, so existing v2 plugins still load. The `OpInfo` layout is unchanged.
- **whitelisted MLIR symbols**: Each whitelisted dialect TypeID exists once in the host `.so`. Type identity is consistent inside one MLIRContext.
- **Python bindings**: The host and the plugin share `libnanobind.so`. IR objects can cross the `.so` boundary, and Python can use the plugin submodule `ir._ascend` directly.

## 3. Implementation

### 3.1 Support MLIR whitelist: Keeping Linalg/Tensor and related symbols

The whitelist `python/src/plugin_ext_dialects.whitelist` names the MLIR dialects whose TypeIDs must be exported. Each line has three columns: CMake target, header, and C++ type.

```text
# format: cmake_target|include_header|TypeExpr
MLIRLinalgDialect|mlir/Dialect/Linalg/IR/Linalg.h|mlir::linalg::LinalgDialect
MLIRTensorDialect|mlir/Dialect/Tensor/IR/Tensor.h|mlir::tensor::TensorDialect
MLIRComplexDialect|mlir/Dialect/Complex/IR/Complex.h|mlir::complex::ComplexDialect
MLIRBufferizationDialect|mlir/Dialect/Bufferization/IR/Bufferization.h|mlir::bufferization::BufferizationDialect
```

`CMakeLists.txt` reads the whitelist and does two things:

1. Collect the CMake targets into `TRITON_PLUGIN_EXT_DIALECT_LIBS` and, on GNU ld, link them into `libtriton.so` with `--whole-archive`.
2. Generate `plugin_ext_dialects.gen.cc`

items.title: [Gateway] Add routing support for the /v1/audio/speech API
items.author: googs1025
items.body_excerpt:
Parent issue: #2989

## Background

AIBrix documents vLLM-Omni as exposing OpenAI-compatible multimodal APIs, including `/v1/audio/speech`. The Gateway currently supports audio transcription and translation but not speech generation.

Speech generation has a different transport contract: a JSON request, a binary audio response, potentially multiple streamed response chunks, no JSON usage or SSE processing, and no async job registration.

## Proposed behavior

Support `POST /v1/audio/speech`.

The Gateway should:

1. parse the JSON request;
2. require a non-empty `model`;
3. require a non-empty textual `input`;
4. preserve all other request fields;
5. use existing non-PD model routing;
6. stream successful binary responses without parsing or mutation;
7. preserve upstream audio headers.

## Validation

Add a focused validator such as:

```go
func validateAudioSpeechRequest(
    requestID string,
    requestBody []byte,
) (model, message string, errRes *extProcPb.ProcessingResponse)
```

Validate only a JSON object root, a non-empty string `model`, and a non-empty string `input`.

Forward fields such as `voice`, `response_format`, `speed`, `instructions`, `language`, and `stream_format` without duplicating engine validation. A request-level `stream` field must not cause the Gateway to interpret the response as SSE.

## Response handling

Classify `/v1/audio/speech` as a non-language response.

Do not pass successful binary responses through language JSON parsing, SSE parsing, token usage extraction, video job rewriting, or full response buffering.

Preserve `Content-Type`, `Content-Length`, `Content-Disposition`, and `Transfer-Encoding`. Do not invent token usage for audio output.

## Envoy routing

Add the endpoint to path constants, JSON validation dispatch, non-language response classification, ModelRouter default paths, the shared reserved HTTPRoute, and vLLM-Omni documentation.

No dedicated EnvoyExtensionPolicy is needed because the shared route already streams response bodies.

## Testing

Cover valid requests, field preservation, invalid model/input, malformed JSON, query parameters, model routing, binary and invalid UTF-8 payloads, multi-chunk responses, content header preservation, upstream JSON errors, cancellation and cleanup, no token parsing, no video job registration, and reserved/model route presence.

## Non-goals

- Do not implement speech synthesis in AIBrix.
- Do not add multipart input.
- Do not buffer the complete audio response.
- Do not add async speech jobs.
- Do not add PD support.
- Do not add a dedicated response mode or HTTPRoute.
- Do not change transcription or translation behavior.
- Do not introduce an endpoint registry.

## Acceptance criteria

- Speech requests route by model to an eligible backend Pod.
- Unknown engine-specific fields remain intact.
- Successful audio responses stream byte-for-byte.
- Binary responses never enter JSON or SSE processing.
- Audio response headers are preserved.
- Error, cancellation, and cleanup behavior is tested.
- Both reserved and model routes expose the endpoint.

items.title: [Bug]: MiniMax-M3 NVFP4 produces garbage output + CUDA illegal memory access on Hopper (sm90) via Marlin FP4-MoE
items.author: mikekg
items.body_excerpt:
### Summary

Serving **MiniMax-M3-NVFP4** on **Hopper GPUs (H100 / H200, sm90)** loads and starts the server, but the FP4-MoE forward pass is broken in two independent ways:

1. **Incoherent output** — every request returns garbage (null bytes / repeated-token soup) instead of real text, even at concurrency 1.
2. **CUDA illegal memory access** — the engine crashes at concurrency ≈ 8 inside `fused_marlin_moe`, killing the worker (`EngineDeadError`).

Both reproduce on the **v0.25.1 release** and on the current **nightly**. On Hopper the NVFP4-MoE selector falls back to **MARLIN** (the FlashInfer FP4 backends are Blackwell/SM100-only), and the Marlin FP4-MoE path is where both failures originate.

### Environment

- vLLM **v0.25.1** (also reproduced on a current nightly)
- GPU: **NVIDIA H200** and **H100** (Hopper, sm90)
- Model: `MiniMax-M3-NVFP4` (ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoint; `hidden_act="swigluoai"`, `swiglu_limit` set)
- Selected backend (log): `Using 'MARLIN' NvFp4 MoE backend out of potential backends: ['FLASHINFER_TRTLLM', 'FLASHINFER_CUTLASS', 'MARLIN']`

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
vllm serve MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --trust-remote-code
```

```bash
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "MiniMax-M3-NVFP4",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of France?"}],
  "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 64 }'
```

**At concurrency 1:** the completion is garbage — e.g. 64× ``, or repeated-token soup like `" |,,,, | |,Cut,, Ta,,…"` — never "Paris". The same corruption appears via `/v1/completions` (no chat template), so the defect is in the forward pass, not templating.

**At concurrency ≈ 8:**

```
CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
  ... vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/marlin_moe.py
  ... vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/marlin_utils.py
EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue.
```

### Expected behavior

M3-NVFP4 serves coherent output on Hopper and remains stable across concurrency (no illegal memory access).

### Root cause

Hopper has no native FP4, so a clamped NVFP4-MoE model (M3 sets `swiglu_limit`) is routed to the **Marlin** weight-only path (enabled for non-Blackwell by #45836). That path has two independent defects for M3:

1. **Garbage output** — the Marlin MoE adapter substitutes plain-SiLU defaults instead of forwarding the model's **`swigluoai` activation parameters (alpha / beta / clamp)**. With the wrong activation the MoE output is numerically meaningless.
2. **Illegal memory access** — gated NVFP4/FP8 MoE whose **`moe_intermediate_size` is not aligned** to the Marlin kernel tile pads incorrectly, producing an out-of-bounds access under load (surfaces at concurrency ≈ 8).

The Marlin epilogue additionally mis-indexes per-row top-k weights (#48895) — the shared kernel-level defect — and M3's tile geometry is what turns it into an out-of-bounds access.

### The fix — two open PRs

Two independent fixes are needed; each addresses one symptom, and **both** are required (one alone is insufficient):

| PR | Resolves | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| **#48929** | the **garbage output** | Forwards M3's `swigluoai` activation parameters (alpha / beta / clamp) to the Marlin MoE adapter, instead of substituting plain-SiLU defaults |
| **#48624** | the **illegal memory access** | Pads the gated-MoE intermediate when `moe_intermediate_size` isn't aligned to the Marlin kernel tile |

Both target `main` and are currently open. Applying both over v0.25.1 makes M3 serve coherently (correct "Paris"; correct Rayleigh-scattering explanation) and pass concurrency 8 with no illegal-memory-access, on the same MARLIN backend.

### Related

- **#48895** — Marlin `moe_wna16_marlin_gemm` mis-indexes per-row top-k weights (shared kernel-level defect)
- **#45836** — enabled Marlin-with-clamp on non-Blackwell (merged v0.24.0), which opened this path without the correctness/alignment fixes above

items.title: [Bug]: trtllm-gen FMHA JIT (NVRTC) fails for MLA generation kernels on SM107: ptxas register allocation (grouped BF16) and "Array.cpp:376 Out-of-bound access" (FP8 KV)
items.author: lucifer1004
items.body_excerpt:
### System Info

SM107, TensorRT-LLM main, trtllm-gen FMHA through `TllmGenFmhaRunner` (MLA generation, `HQk 576 / HV 512`, one KV head, paged KV). Configurations that have no precompiled cubin go through the JIT path (`generateAndCompileKernel`).

### Who can help?

@pengbowang-nv

### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [x] My own modified scripts

### Reproduction

Both cases come from a standalone `TllmGenFmhaRunner` microbenchmark using the same runner parameters as `AttentionOp`'s MLA generation path.

1. BF16 Q/KV/O, grouped MLA generation (`FmhaOptions::mSelectsGroupedMla = true`), 64 tokens per page (no grouped cubin exists for page 64, so it goes to NVRTC). The autotuner picks KeepsMmaAb, tileSizeQ 64, tileSizeKv 128, groupsTokensHeadsQ, HVPerCta 256. Compilation fails with:

   ~~~
   ptxas fatal : (C7600) Register allocation failed with register count of '176'
   ~~~

   The precompiled page-32 cubins of the same kernel family (`fmhaSm107aKernel_...PagedKvCausalP32...Q64Kv128...GroupedKeepsAbForGen`) run fine.

2. FP8 (e4m3) Q and KV, BF16 output, non-grouped MLA generation, causal, 32 tokens per page, 16 heads, batch 1, with 32 or 2048 query tokens per request. No cubin exists for these, and the generator aborts:

   ~~~
   [E] [Array.cpp:376]: Out-of-bound access
   terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
     what():  Out-of-bound access
   ~~~

   For comparison, with grouped selection and 1, 8 or 16 query tokens (batch 1 to 16), the precompiled grouped FP8 cubins are found and run normally.

### Expected behavior

The JIT path either produces a working kernel or reports cleanly that the configuration is unsupported, so the caller can choose a different kernel.

### actual behavior

Case 1: ptxas fails during the build. Case 2: the generator throws from inside the library, and the process terminates.

### additional notes

Both failures are inside the binary trtllm-gen generator, so I cannot propose a fix in this repository. Case 1 is only reachable with grouped MLA selection enabled, which main does not do (#15009, #20375, #20376).

comments.author: lucifer1004
comments.body:
Related: #20382 (FP8-KV grouped MLA generation hangs on SM107 when heads per rank do not divide 64, e.g. 12).

I think case 2 here (FP8 non-grouped, including the 2048-query-token shape) is likely the same gap seen from the other side: SM107 has no SwapsAb E4M3 MLA generation cubin, so those shapes go to NVRTC and fail, while the grouped E4M3 cubins that do exist hang for head counts that do not divide the 64-row Q tile. So right now FP8 MLA generation on SM107 seems to work only with grouped selection and 4/8/16/32 heads per rank.

items.title: GLM-5.3 (glm_moe_dsa) emits repeated '@' tokens instead of a response on CPU (ngl=0)
items.author: darkhipo
items.body_excerpt:
## Summary

Serving **GLM-5.3** (`glm_moe_dsa`, unsloth/GLM-5.3-GGUF `UD-Q4_K_XL`) on CPU produces only repeated `@` tokens in `reasoning_content` and no answer. Reproduced twice. Root cause not yet isolated — filing with symptom + repro so it can be triaged.

## Environment

- llama.cpp master @ `7ceed87` (2026-09-16), Metal build, **CPU inference only** (`-ngl 0`)
- macOS (M4 Max, 128 GB)
- Model: `unsloth/GLM-5.3-GGUF` → `UD-Q4_K_XL` (11 shards; shard 1 is the 9.4 MB metadata-only shard)

## Repro

```
llama-server \
  -m /path/to/GLM-5.3-UD-Q4_K_XL-00001-of-00011.gguf \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8113 \
  --load-mode mmap -fit off -c 2048 -ngl 0 -t 8 -np 1 \
  --no-warmup --cache-type-k q4_0 --cache-type-v q4_0 --no-repack \
  --reasoning on --reasoning-format deepseek --reasoning-effort low
```

Then POST `/v1/chat/completions`:

```json
{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi!"}],"max_tokens":256,"temperature":0.0}
```

## Actual

```
message.reasoning_content = "@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@ ..." (128 '@' tokens)
message.content          = ""
finish_reason            = length
```

The model never produces the `<think>…</think>` block or an answer — it degenerates to repeating a single `@` token.

## Expected

`<think>…</think>` reasoning followed by a normal greeting (the model's own chat template, see below).

## What I've already ruled out

- **Not a missing chat template.** The GGUF *does* embed a chat template (jinja), and `[gMASK]`/`<sop>`/`<eop>`/`<|user|>`/`<|assistant|>`/`<|system|>`/`<|observation|>` are all present in the vocab. Serving with `--chat-template-file` (the `zai-org/GLM-5.3/chat_template.jinja`) + `--reasoning-format deepseek` + low effort still yields `@`.
- **Not a truncated download.** Every shard size matches the HF API exactly; shard 1 (9,428,677 bytes) is metadata-only by design.
- **The `@` token is shared with GLM-5.2** (also present in the GLM-5.2 tokenizer), so it looks like a GLM control/thinking token that is leaking instead of being driven correctly.

## Open question (why I can't state the root cause)

I attempted the same CPU test against **GLM-5.2** (`glm_moe_dsa`, same arch) to see whether this is GLM-5.3-specific or general `glm_moe_dsa`. That run did not emit `@` but also produced no response within 30 min — however the host was under heavy concurrent disk I/O (multi-TB model downloads), so the GLM-5.2 result is confounded and not conclusive. I did not want to claim a general `glm_moe_dsa` bug on that basis.

## Likely suspects (for a maintainer with arch context)

- `glm-dsa` expert-group handling (`glm-dsa.expert_group_count` / `expert_group_used_count` / `expert_gating_func` in the GGUF metadata) — if GLM-5.3 introduced grouped experts that the GLM-5.2-era `glm_moe_dsa` path doesn't fully drive.
- The `[gMASK]<sop>` generation-mask prefix not being applied, leaving the model with a malformed prompt and causing it to fall into a degenerate repeat of its control token.

Happy to provide `--verbose` logs, a tokenizer dump, or run any suggested experiment.

items.title: heterodyne: per-token and per-layer diff of two llama.cpp runs via cb_eval, with activation transplants
items.author: zaydmulani09
items.body_excerpt:
I built a tool on top of llama.cpp (pinned at b11696, CPU backend, static) that runs two configurations on identical tokens and compares them per position and per layer: https://github.com/zaydmulani09/heterodyne

It uses `cb_eval` to capture or overwrite `l_out-N` and `ffn_inp-N` with `ggml_backend_tensor_get/set`, tracking rows per ubatch and checking that every row of every hooked tensor was seen. That lets it write one run's residual stream into another and measure what KL is left, layer by layer, and between each layer's attention and MLP.

One observation that might interest people here: on CPU, with flash attention off, Q4_K_M output was bitwise identical across ubatch sizes that are multiples of 4 and not otherwise (ubatch 62, 63, 65 changed 3 to 5% of top-1 tokens on a 128-token chunk). The repacked K-quant matmul seems to explain it: it quantizes activation rows in interleaved groups of 4 and sends the remainder through a separate path (ggml/src/ggml-cpu/repack.cpp:4697-4702 at b11696). With flash attention on, every weight type changed with the ubatch size. llama-perplexity agrees (Q4_K_M, ubatch 57 vs 114: KLD 0.0057). I don't think this is a bug, but it matters for anyone comparing runs, so heterodyne measures a floor with an odd split.

Related: there's no public API for per-layer hidden states (#27112), which is why this goes through cb_eval and graph tensor names. Feedback welcome, especially on whether those names are stable enough to rely on across architectures.

items.title: json-schema-to-grammar: `minLength`/`maxLength` silently dropped when the string also has a `pattern`
items.author: amitabhsh
items.body_excerpt:
### What happens

For a string schema that has both a `pattern` and a length bound, the generated
grammar encodes only the pattern. The length bound disappears, and no warning is
printed.

```json
{"type": "string", "pattern": "^[a-z]+$", "maxLength": 4}
```

The grammar that llama-server builds (`POST /completion` with `n_predict: 0`,
`json_schema` set to the schema above, and
`response_fields: ["generation_settings/grammar"]`):

```
root ::= "\"" ([a-z]+) "\""
space ::= | " " | "\n"{1,2} [ \t]{0,20}
```

The grammar accepts `"abcdefgh"`, but the schema rejects it (`maxLength: 4`).

### Why

In `common/json-schema-to-grammar.cpp` (master at `eb1e1f495f`, 2026-09-19),
`visit()`'s `KIND_STRING` branch returns from the `pattern` case before it gets
to the length case:

```cpp
if (!str.pattern.empty()) {
    return _visit_pattern(str.pattern, rule_name);   // returns here
}
...
if (str.min_length > 0 || str.max_length >= 0) {     // never reached with a pattern
```

Unlike an unsupported regex, this path adds nothing to `_warnings`, so neither
the Python converter's warnings nor the server log mention it. The README's
"known limitations" list doesn't mention it either.

### How common it is

Pydantic and similar generators routinely emit `pattern` together with
`min_length`/`max_length` (for example `constr(pattern=..., max_length=...)`).
In a fuzzed corpus of 200 schemas, a grammar-constrained `qwen2.5:1.5b` broke
the length bound on 9 of the 71 length-under-pattern instances. It broke zero
of the length bounds the grammar did encode.

### Possible fixes

1. At minimum, push a warning when `pattern` and `minLength`/`maxLength` appear
   together, matching what XGrammar does
   (`pattern combined with minLength/maxLength is not supported; ignoring minLength/maxLength`).
2. Enforce both. A length-bounded `char` repetition and the pattern rule can't
   be intersected in GBNF in general, but the common case of a pattern that is a
   single repeated character class (`^[a-z]+$`, `^\w{3,16}$`) can be rewritten
   by intersecting the repetition bounds.
3. llama.cpp builds with `LLAMA_USE_LLGUIDANCE` already enforce both; llguidance
   1.9.1 rejected every length-under-pattern violation in the same test.

### Environment

- llama.cpp `common/json-schema-to-grammar.cpp` at `eb1e1f495f` (read
  2026-10-17). Reproduced on the llama-server vendored in Ollama 0.40.5.
- Found with a property-based fuzzer that plants keyword interactions; the
  model-free acceptance check, corpus and scripts are available on request.

items.title: [Bug]: [TransferEngine] HTTP metadata server rejects valid rpc_meta republish as duplicate
items.author: thrower01
items.body_excerpt:
### Bug Report

Context

The Python HTTP metadata backend (`python/mooncake/http_metadata_server.py` ) is a lightweight alternative to etcd/Redis for Mooncake Transfer Engine deployments. On the C++ side,`TransferMetadata::rePublishRpcMetaEntry` (in`mooncake-transfer-engine/src/transfer_metadata.cpp:1928` ) implements a versioned idempotency rule: if the same`(ip_or_host_name, rpc_port)` publishes again, the client bumps`metadata_version` and PUTs the new JSON. This is the normal path for process restart, multi-worker duplicate registration, and any republish scenario.

The current Python server gates`rpc_meta` keys with two bugs, and together they make a legitimate republish always fail.

Bug 1 — substring match is too broad


`if key.find("rpc_meta") != -1 and key in self.store:`

A key such as`mooncake/segment_rpc_meta_cache/x` is NOT an rpc_meta key, but the substring check pulls it into the gate. Non-rpc_meta business keys whose names happen to contain`rpc_meta` can no longer be overwritten.

Bug 2 — byte-level equality rejects version bumps


`if self.store[key] == data: return 200
return 400 "Duplicate rpc_meta key not allowed"`

The C++ client always increments`metadata_version` on republish, so the new payload bytes are never byte-identical to the existing value. Every valid republish is treated as a duplicate conflict.

Impact

Any cluster using the HTTP metadata server will get 400 responses when clients republish their own rpc_meta (process restart, duplicate registration), forcing the client into retry or misleading the operator into thinking the metadata backend is broken. Non-rpc_meta keys whose name merely contains the substring can also stop being writable.

Fix direction

- Classify rpc_meta keys by path-segment membership: split on`/` , require`"rpc_meta"` as a literal segment.
- Replace byte-level equality with a JSON-aware rule:
  - identical bytes → idempotent accept
  - `metadata_version` strictly increasing and`(ip_or_host_name, rpc_port)` unchanged → accept overwrite
  - `metadata_version` rollback or identity-field conflict → 400 with a machine-readable reason
Scope of fix

The same broken gate is also copied into`mooncake-transfer-engine/example/http-metadata-server-python/bootstrap_server.py` (the example had the older version that rejected ALL duplicate rpc_meta keys, not even allowing idempotent same-byte writes). Both need updating.

Acceptance

- New unit tests for substring false-positive, version-bump acceptance, rollback rejection, identity-conflict rejection. Existing same-byte idempotency / conflict tests keep passing.
- Semantics aligned with`TransferMetadata::rePublishRpcMetaEntry` .

### Before submitting...

- [x] Ensure you searched for relevant issues and read the [documentation]

items.title: Why does num_warps affect numerical precision?
items.author: yaozhenghangma
items.body_excerpt:
I'm testing a Flash Attention kernel, and I've placed the test code at the end. In short, when performing an attention operation using q, k, and v matrices with `num_batchs = 8`, `seq_len = 128`, `num_heads = 128`, and `head_dim = 128`, I observed that setting `num_warps = 4` and `num_warps = 8` produce different output results. The maximum difference between the output matrices is `0.00048828125`, and this difference remains consistent across repeated runs. Moreover, when keeping all other parameters the same and setting `seq_len` to 32 or smaller, the discrepancy disappears. 

I'm using an Nvidia T4 GPU, with CUDA version 12.4 and Triton version 3.1.0.

```python
import math
import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl


@triton.jit
def flash_attention_kernel(
    q_ptr, k_ptr, v_ptr, o_ptr,
    start_loc, seq_len,
    q_stride_batch_seq, q_stride_head, q_stride_dim,
    k_stride_batch_seq, k_stride_head, k_stride_dim,
    v_stride_batch_seq, v_stride_head, v_stride_dim,
    o_stride_batch_seq, o_stride_head, o_stride_dim,
    num_head,
    kv_group_size,
    d_scale,
    BLOCK_SIZE_M: tl.constexpr,
    BLOCK_SIZE_N: tl.constexpr,
    BLOCK_SIZE_D: tl.constexpr
):
    # q k v: [batchs*seq, heads, dim]
    q_block_id = tl.program_id(0) # m id
    batch_and_head_id = tl.program_id(1)
    batch_id = batch_and_head_id // num_head
    head_id = batch_and_head_id % num_head
    kv_head_id = head_id // kv_group_size

    batch_start = tl.load(start_loc + batch_id)
    batch_seq_len = tl.load(seq_len + batch_id)

    m_ranges = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE_M)
    n_ranges = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE_N)
    m_start = q_block_id * BLOCK_SIZE_M
    m_offsets = m_ranges + m_start
    embed_offsets = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE_D)

    q_offsets = (
        (batch_start + m_offsets[:,None]) * q_stride_batch_seq
        + head_id * q_stride_head
        + embed_offsets[None,:] * q_stride_dim
    )

    k_offsets = (
        (batch_start + n_ranges[:,None]) * k_stride_batch_seq
        + kv_head_id * k_stride_head
        + embed_offsets[None,:] * k_stride_dim
    )

    v_offsets = (
        (batch_start + n_ranges[:,None]) * v_stride_batch_seq
        + kv_head_id * v_stride_head
        + embed_offsets[None,:] * v_stride_dim
    )

    o_offsets = (
        (batch_start + m_offsets[:,None]) * o_stride_batch_seq
        + head_id * o_stride_head
        + embed_offsets[None,:] * o_stride_dim
    )

    q_mask = m_offsets[:,None]  < batch_seq_len
    q = tl.load(q_ptr + q_offsets, mask=q_mask, other=0.0)

    acc = tl.zeros((BLOCK_SIZE_M, BLOCK_SIZE_D), dtype=tl.float32)
    m_i = tl.zeros((BLOCK_SIZE_M,), dtype=tl.float32) - float("inf")
    l_i = tl.zeros((BLOCK_SIZE_M,), dtype=tl.float32)

    m_mask = tl.where(m_start < batch_seq_len, 1, 0) # loop for m > seq_len is ignored
    n_size = tl.minimum(m_start + BLOCK_SIZE_M, batch_seq_len) # inter block casual mask

    for n_idx in range(0, n_size * m_mask, BLOCK_SIZE_N):
        k_mask = n_idx + n_ranges[:,None] < n_size
        k = tl.load(k_ptr + k_offsets + n_idx * k_stride_batch_seq, mask=k_mask, other=0.0)
        v = tl.load(v_ptr + v_offsets + n_idx * v_stride_batch_seq, mask=k_mask, other=0.0)

        qk = tl.zeros((BLOCK_SIZE_M, BLOCK_SIZE_N), dtype=tl.float32)
        qk += tl.dot(q, tl.trans(k))

        # intra block casual mask
        q_off = m_offsets
        k_off = n_idx + n_ranges
        mask = q_off[:,None] >= k_off[None,:]
        qk = tl.where(mask, qk * d_scale, -float("inf"))

        pad_mask = n_idx + n_ranges < n_size
        qk = tl.where(pad_mask[None,:], qk, -float("inf"))

        m_j = tl.max(qk, axis=1)
        m_new = tl.maximum(m_i, m_j)
        alpha = tl.exp2(m_i - m_new)

        P_j = tl.exp2(qk - m_new[:,None])
        l_j = tl.sum(P_j, axis=1)
        l_i = l_i * alpha + l_j

        o_scale = alpha
        acc = acc * o_scale[:, None]
        P_j = P_j.to(v_ptr.dtype.element_ty)
        acc += tl.dot(P_j, v)

        m_i = m_new

    acc = acc / l_i[:, None]

    tl.store(o_ptr + o_offsets, acc, mask=q_mask)


def flash_attention(q: torch.Tensor, k, v, start_loc, seq_len, num_warps):
    _, num_head, d_size = q.shape
    _, num_kv_head, _ = k.shape
    kv_group_size = num_head // num_kv_head
    num_batch = seq_len.shape[0]
    max_seq_len = int(torch.max(seq_len).item())
    d_scale = 1.0 / math.sqrt(d_size) * 1.4426950408889634

    grid = lambda meta: (
        triton.cdiv(max_seq_len, meta["BLOCK_SIZE_M"]),
        num_batch * num_head,
        1
    )
    num_stages = 1

    o = torch.empty_like(q, dtype=q.dtype, device=q.device)
    flash_attention_kernel[grid](
        q, k, v, o,
        start_loc, seq_len,
        *q.stride(), *k.stride(), *v.stride(), *o.stride(),
        num_head=num_head,
        kv_group_size=kv_group_size,
        d_scale=d_scale,
        BLOCK_SIZE_M=64,
        BLOCK_SIZE_N=64,
        BLOCK_SIZE_D=d_size,
        num_warps=num_warps,
        num_stages=num_stages,
    )

    return o

items.title: Constexprs that compare equal but differ in type or sign (1 and 1.0, 0.0 and -0.0) reuse each other's binary
items.author: shuyilinn
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

When a kernel is launched with a constexpr that compares equal to the value of an earlier launch but has a different type or sign (`1` and `1.0`, or `0.0` and `-0.0`), the second launch reuses the binary compiled for the first one. The result depends on which value was launched first.

```python
import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl


@triton.jit
def kernel(X, out, C: tl.constexpr):
    tl.store(out, tl.load(X) * C)


x = torch.tensor([2**30 + 1], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
for order in [(1, 1.0), (1.0, 1)]:
    kernel.device_caches.clear()
    results = []
    for c in order:
        out = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
        kernel[(1, )](x, out, c)
        results.append(out.item())
    print(order, results)
```

```
(1, 1.0) [1073741825, 1073741825]
(1.0, 1) [1073741824, 1073741824]
```

Expected: `x * 1` is `1073741825` and `x * 1.0` (computed in fp32) is `1073741824`, regardless of launch order. In the same way, launching with `C=0.0` and then `C=-0.0` stores `0.0` for the second launch.

The on-disk cache is not affected: the string key built from the specialization differs (`1` vs `1.0`, `0.0` vs `-0.0`). The problem is the in-memory lookup in `compute_cache_key` (`python/triton/runtime/jit.py`):

```python
key = (tuple(specialization), str(options))
cache_key = kernel_key_cache.get(key, None)
```

The specialization contains `("constexpr", value)`, and tuple equality treats `1 == 1.0 == True` and `0.0 == -0.0` (with equal hashes) as the same key, so the string key of the first launch is returned. This cache was added in #7768.

### Environment details

Triton: main @ 41846bc965
GPU: NVIDIA RTX 4090 (sm_89), driver 570 / CUDA 12.8

items.title: `tl.reduce` over a tuple with `axis=None` pairs values with the wrong indices
items.author: shuyilinn
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

`tl.reduce` over a tuple with `axis=None` can pair values with the wrong indices. An argmax written as `tl.reduce((x, idx), None, combine)` returns the right maximum but the wrong index. The same reduction with `axis=0` on the same 1-D input is correct.

```python
import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl


@triton.jit
def combine(v1, i1, v2, i2):
    gt = (v1 > v2) | ((v1 == v2) & (i1 < i2))
    return tl.where(gt, v1, v2), tl.where(gt, i1, i2)


@triton.jit
def argmax(X, O, N: tl.constexpr, AXIS_NONE: tl.constexpr):
    off = tl.arange(0, N)
    x = tl.load(X + off)
    if AXIS_NONE:
        v, i = tl.reduce((x, off), None, combine)
    else:
        v, i = tl.reduce((x, off), 0, combine)
    tl.store(O, i)
    tl.store(O + 1, v)


N = 1024
torch.manual_seed(0)
x = torch.randperm(N, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
for axis_none in (False, True):
    o = torch.zeros(2, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
    argmax[(1, )](x, o, N, axis_none, num_warps=4)
    print(f"axis={'None' if axis_none else 0}: max={o[1].item()} index={o[0].item()} (expected index {x.argmax().item()})")
```

```
axis=0: max=1023 index=535 (expected index 535)
axis=None: max=1023 index=901 (expected index 535)
```

For `axis=None`, `reduction` in `python/triton/language/semantic.py` flattens each operand separately with `reshape(..., can_reorder=True)`. The two reshapes are free to reorder their elements independently, and here the loaded `x` and the `arange` end up in different orders, so the combine function sees `x[p]` together with `idx[q]`, `q != p`.

This is the same failure as #12099; its fix (#12124) covers the reshape the compiler inserts, not this frontend path. Reshaping the operands with `can_reorder=False`, or reshaping them together, would keep the pairing.

### Environment details

Triton: main @ 41846bc965
GPU: NVIDIA RTX 4090 (sm_89), driver 570 / CUDA 12.8

items.title: fp64 downcast with `fp_downcast_rounding="rtz"` fails with "Unsupported rounding mode for conversion"
items.author: shuyilinn
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

Casting fp64 to fp32, fp16 or bf16 with `fp_downcast_rounding="rtz"` fails to compile with `LLVM ERROR: Unsupported rounding mode for conversion.` The frontend accepts it, and the `cast` docstring documents `fp_downcast_rounding` for any float downcast. The interpreter computes the right result.

```python
import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl


@triton.jit
def cast_rtz(X, Y):
    offs = tl.arange(0, 16)
    tl.store(Y + offs, tl.load(X + offs).to(Y.dtype.element_ty, fp_downcast_rounding="rtz"))


x = torch.full((16, ), 1 + 2**-30, dtype=torch.float64, device="cuda")
y = torch.zeros(16, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")
cast_rtz[(1, )](x, y)
print(y[0].item())
```

```
Unsupported conversion from f64 to f16 with rounding mode rtz
LLVM ERROR: Unsupported rounding mode for conversion.
...
RuntimeError: PassManager::run failed
```

Expected `1.0`. fp16 and bf16 destinations fail the same way; the message names f16 for the fp32 destination as well.

For a non-default rounding mode, `cast` in `python/triton/language/semantic.py` emits `tt.fp_to_fp` with that mode, but `FpToFpOpConversion` (`third_party/nvidia/lib/TritonNVIDIAGPUToLLVM/ElementwiseOpToLLVM.cpp`) has no conversion with an f64 source. With the default RTNE the frontend emits `arith.truncf` instead, which works. For fp32, PTX has `cvt.rz.f32.f64`.

### Environment details

Triton: main @ 41846bc965
GPU: NVIDIA RTX 4090 (sm_89), driver 570 / CUDA 12.8

items.title: [Feature]: Skip unused history for single-token beam stop words
items.author: yifanQi98
items.body_excerpt:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

`FinishReasonsHandler._get_past_tokens()` materializes `request.get_tokens()`, builds one CPU history tensor per beam, and copies the result to CUDA even when every stop word of a beam-search request is a single token. Matching those stop words only needs the newly generated token.

I propose a small early return for beam-search requests whose nonempty stop-word list contains only single-token words. Allocate zero history directly on CUDA, preserving the handler-wide `[max_stop_word_length - 1, max_beam_width]` shape. Preserve the existing history path for multi-token stop words and single-beam requests. In mixed batches, shorter stop words are left-padded and their history positions are masked by the existing matcher.

The redundant work remains on `main` at `9e8e5a270ecd03919f914680581f8c1cc4e5bf25`. The affected source file is byte-identical to the installed TensorRT-LLM 1.4.0rc0 file used for validation.

An isolated prototype on Qwen3-0.6B / BF16 / RTX PRO 5000 72GB Blackwell reduced complete `LLM.generate` latency by 2.89% (3 output tokens, submitted batch 1), 4.17% (3 tokens, batch 2), and 1.64% (8 tokens, batch 2), with beam capacity 500 and variable beam widths. Six independent baseline/candidate process pairs alternated AB/BA order; each case had 10 warmups and 60 timed calls. These are closed-loop latency measurements, not fixed-QPS or saturated-throughput results. A multi-token-stop fallback control showed no measurable gain.

This saves work during request admission/history reprocessing, not at every decode step. It does not change EOS/stop semantics. With the current request conversion, `ignore_eos=True` clears stop words, so this path is not called and there is no benefit.

### Alternatives

Keep the existing implementation; or optimize general multi-token history materialization separately. This proposal keeps the multi-token path unchanged and introduces no public setting or kernel.

### Additional context

I have prepared a focused implementation and regression tests covering stop hits/misses, mixed single-/multi-token requests, finish-reason precedence, buffer growth, and slot reuse. I will link the implementation PR here through its issue reference. No API-stability reference change is needed.

        img2 = tl.load(img2_item_ptrs, mask=mask, other=0)
        out = ratio * img1 + (1.0 - ratio) * img2
        tl.store(img1_item_ptrs, out, mask=mask)
    else:
        img1 = tl.load(img1_item_ptrs)
        img2 = tl.load(img2_item_ptrs)
        out = ratio * img1 + (1.0 - ratio) * img2
        tl.store(img1_item_ptrs, out)
```

Given that this kernel is blending 2 uint8  tensors, I figured it would make sense to do the computation ` out = ratio * img1 + (1.0 - ratio) * img2`  since I don't need high precision.

However, I can't figure out how to force the Triton compiler to do the computations in FP16.
I tried doing:

```python3
        img1 = tl.load(img1_item_ptrs, mask=mask, other=0).to(tl.float16)
        img2 = tl.load(img2_item_ptrs, mask=mask, other=0).to(tl.float16)
```
but from looking at the generated PTX, it just seems like the float16s are just converted to float32s before the multiplication 
occurs.

Is there a way I can force the Triton  compiler  to make the multiplications float16? (Or is this impossible for a good reason;  i.e maybe this is not what I actually want)?

items.title: [WS] getPartitionOutputs assertion in NVWSHoistTmemStore with warp_specialize=True on a pointer-load persistent matmul
items.author: builtin-pb
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

Compiling the kernel below for Blackwell (`cuda:100` or `cuda:103`) stops with an internal assertion when the outer tile loop uses `tl.range(..., warp_specialize=True)`, the inner K loop uses plain pointer loads and `tl.dot`, and C is written with a plain `tl.store`:

```
Partitioning.cpp:24: ... mlir::triton::gpu::getPartitionOutputs(mlir::Operation*): Assertion `op->hasAttr(kPartitionOutputsAttrName)' failed.
... Pipeline failed while executing [`TritonGPUAutomaticWarpSpecialization` on 'builtin.module' operation, `NVWSHoistTmemStore` on 'builtin.module' operation]
RuntimeError: PassManager::run failed
```

This reproduces on Triton 3.8.0 (PyPI wheel; there the assertion is at `Partition.cpp:354`) and on main (`0d4e0a0c`). It is compile-only and needs no GPU; the kernel is never launched (it assumes full tiles and 16-byte-aligned, contiguous fp16 A and B and fp32 C). We are not asking for this loop to be specialized, only for no assertion: `warp_specialize` is documented as an attempt, and loops it cannot partition are otherwise left alone, as with the controls below. Triton's own `test_warp_specialize_tma_matmul_persistent` has the same structure with pointer loads for A and B and expects `ttg.warp_specialize`; it differs only in storing C through a descriptor.

### Reproducer

```python
"""Compile-only reproducer (no GPU needed).

Requesting automatic warp specialization on a persistent tile loop whose body is
an ordinary pointer-load matmul makes Triton hit an internal assertion:
    getPartitionOutputs: Assertion `op->hasAttr(kPartitionOutputsAttrName)' failed.

    python ws_assert_min.py              # warp_specialize=True: assertion
    python ws_assert_min.py --ws 0       # same kernel without it: compiles

--inner 0 drops the inner K loop (one tl.dot per tile); --dot 0 replaces tl.dot
with row/column sums; --cdesc 1 stores C through a TMA tensor descriptor
(as Triton's own persistent warp-specialization test does); --arch picks the target (100 = B200, 103 = B300, 90 = H100);
--warps and --stages set num_warps (default 4) and num_stages (default 3).
"""
import argparse
import inspect

import triton
import triton.language as tl
from triton.backends.compiler import GPUTarget
from triton.compiler import ASTSource


@triton.jit
def ws_min(A, B, C, num_tiles, k_iters,
           BM: tl.constexpr, BN: tl.constexpr, BK: tl.constexpr,
           WS: tl.constexpr, INNER: tl.constexpr, DOT: tl.constexpr, CDESC: tl.constexpr):
    rm = tl.arange(0, BM)
    rn = tl.arange(0, BN)
    rk = tl.arange(0, BK)
    K = k_iters * BK
    if CDESC:
        c_desc = tl.make_tensor_descriptor(C, shape=[num_tiles * BM, BN], strides=[BN, 1], block_shape=[BM, BN])
    for tile in tl.range(tl.program_id(0), num_tiles, tl.num_programs(0), warp_specialize=WS):
        rows = tile * BM + rm
        acc = tl.zeros((BM, BN), tl.float32)
        if INNER:
            for k in range(k_iters):
                a = tl.load(A + rows[:, None] * K + (k * BK + rk)[None, :])
                b = tl.load(B + (k * BK + rk)[:, None] * BN + rn[None, :])
                if DOT:
                    acc = tl.dot(a, b, acc)
                else:
                    acc += tl.sum(a.to(tl.float32), 1)[:, None] + tl.sum(b.to(tl.float32), 0)[None, :]
        else:
            a = tl.load(A + rows[:, None] * K + rk[None, :])
            b = tl.load(B + rk[:, None] * BN + rn[None, :])
            if DOT:
                acc = tl.dot(a, b, acc)
            else:
                acc += tl.sum(a.to(tl.float32), 1)[:, None] + tl.sum(b.to(tl.float32), 0)[None, :]
        if CDESC:
            c_desc.store([tile * BM, 0], acc)
        else:
            tl.store(C + rows[:, None] * BN + rn[None, :], acc)


def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument("--ws", type=int, default=1)
    p.add_argument("--inner", type=int, default=1)
    p.add_argument("--dot", type=int, default=1)
    p.add_argument("--cdesc", type=int, default=0)
    p.add_argument("--arch", type=int, default=100)
    p.add_argument("--warps", type=int, default=4)
    p.add_argument("--stages", type=int, default=3)
    args = p.parse_args()

    constants = dict(BM=128, BN=64, BK=64, WS=bool(args.ws), INNER=bool(args.inner), DOT=bool(args.dot), CDESC=bool(args.cdesc))
    runtime = dict(A="*fp16", B="*fp16", C="*fp32", num_tiles="i32", k_iters="i32")
    names = list(ws_min.arg_names)
    signature = {n: runtime.get(n, "constexpr") for n in names}
    attrs = {(names.index(n),): [["tt.divisibility", 16]] for n in ("A", "B", "C")}
    key = "constexprs" if "constexprs" in inspect.signature(ASTSource).parameters else "constants"
    src = ASTSource(ws_min, signature=signature, attrs=attrs, **{key: constants})
    print(f"triton {triton.__version__}, target cuda:{args.arch}, warps {args.warps}, stages {args.stages}, {constants}", flush=True)
    compiled = triton.compile(src, target=GPUTarget("cuda", args.arch, 32),
                              options=dict(num_warps=args.warps, num_stages=args.stages))
    ttgir = compiled.asm["ttgir"]
    print("COMPILED; ttg.warp_specialize ops in TTGIR:", ttgir.count("ttg.warp_specialize("), flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

| Command (`--arch 100` or `--arch 103`) | 3.8.0 and main |
|---|---|
| `python ws_assert_min.py` (also with `--stages 1` or `--warps 8`) | assertion |
| `--ws 0` | compiles |
| `--cdesc 1` (C stored through a tensor descriptor) | compiles and emits one `ttg.warp_specialize` |
| `--inner 0` or `--dot 0` | compiles, without specialization |

<details><summary>Full output on main, including the MLIR reproducer</summary>

```
python: triton/lib/Dialect/TritonGPU/IR/Partitioning.cpp:24: llvm::SmallVector<llvm::SetVector<int, llvm::SmallVector<int, 0>, llvm::DenseSet<int, llvm::DenseMapInfo<int, void> >, 0>, 4> mlir::triton::gpu::getPartitionOutputs(mlir::Operation*): Assertion `op->hasAttr(kPartitionOutputsAttrName)' failed.
module {
  tt.func public @ws_min(%ar

items.title: [Bug][Gateway] Add missing reserved routes for supported Messages and Audio APIs
items.author: googs1025
items.body_excerpt:
Parent issue: #2989

## Problem

The Gateway request parser and ModelRouter already support:

- `/v1/messages`
- `/v1/audio/transcriptions`
- `/v1/audio/translations`

However, these paths are missing from the deployed shared `reserved-router` in `config/gateway/gateway-plugin/gateway-plugin.yaml`.

A request must first match this route to enter the external processing service. The plugin then extracts the model from the request body, writes the internal routing headers, clears the route cache, and rematches the request onto a model route.

Without the first route, the existing parser and ModelRouter support do not form a complete deployment path.

## Proposed change

Add these existing endpoints to the shared reserved route:

```yaml
- path:
    type: PathPrefix
    value: /v1/messages
- path:
    type: PathPrefix
    value: /v1/audio/transcriptions
- path:
    type: PathPrefix
    value: /v1/audio/translations
```

Verify the rendered Kustomize output as well.

## Testing

Add regression tests confirming that:

- all three paths are present in the shared reserved route;
- all three paths use the shared Gateway ext_proc policy;
- `/v1/messages` reaches JSON request-body processing;
- the two audio paths reach multipart request-body processing;
- query strings do not break routing;
- existing Chat, Responses, and Videos routes remain unchanged.

## Non-goals

- Do not change `PathPrefix` to `Exact`.
- Do not add HTTP method matches.
- Do not introduce an endpoint registry.
- Do not add `/v1/audio/speech`; that is tracked separately.
- Do not refactor the existing request dispatcher.

## Acceptance criteria

- Messages requests complete the reserved-route -> ext_proc -> model-route flow.
- Audio transcription and translation requests can extract the multipart model and select a backend Pod.
- Existing routes retain their current behavior.
- Regression tests cover both the deployed route and request-processing entry points.

items.author: nealvaidya
items.body_excerpt:
### Your current environment
Output of vllm collect-env ```text ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 Libc version : glibc-2.39 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.13.0+cu130 Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : 13.0 ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.12.3 (main, Aug 31 2026, 10:18:26) [GCC 13.3.0] (64-bit runtime) Python platform : Linux-7.0.0-1010-oracle-x86_64-with-glibc2.39 ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== Is CUDA available : True CUDA runtime version : 13.0.88 GPU models and configuration : GPU 0: NVIDIA H200 GPU 1: NVIDIA H200 GPU 2: NVIDIA H200 GPU 3: NVIDIA H200 Nvidia driver version : 610.57.04 ============================== Versions of relevant libraries ============================== [pip3] flashinfer-python==0.7.0.post1 [pip3] torch==2.13.0+cu130 [pip3] transformers==5.17.0 [pip3] triton==3.7.1 ============================== vLLM Info ============================== vLLM Version : 0.31.0 vLLM Build Flags: CUDA Archs: 7.5 8.0 8.6 8.9 9.0 10.0 12.0; ROCm: Disabled; XPU: Disabled ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug Loading an MoE model with an expert-score correction bias through the weight cache (`--load-format ipc_cache`) either crashes or fails to start. The same model loads and generates correctly from disk. `IpcModelLoader._apply_entries` replaces each meta placeholder parameter with a new `nn.Parameter` object ([ipc_loader.py#L256-L264](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/ipc_loader.py#L256-L264)). Objects that captured the placeholder while the model was being constructed keep the meta tensor. MoE routers are such objects: - MoE models pass their gate's parameter into the MoE layer, for example `e_score_correction_bias=self.gate.e_score_correction_bias` in [nemotron_h.py#L244](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6/vllm/model_executor/models/nemotron_h.py#L244), [lfm2_moe.py#L155](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6/vllm/model_executor/models/lfm2_moe.py#L155), [deepseek_v2.py#L390](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6/vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_v2.py#L390), and [ernie45_moe.py#L193](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6/vllm/model_executor/models/ernie45_moe.py#L193). - The router keeps that tensor object: [grouped_topk_router.py#L274](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/router/grouped_topk_router.py#L274) and [fused_topk_bias_router.py#L369](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/router/fused_topk_bias_router.py#L369). After `_apply_entries`, the gate holds the cached tensor and every router still holds the meta placeholder. `_apply_entries` is unchanged on `main`. ### Reproduction This needs a single GPU larger than 80 GB (tested on a 141 GB H200). Start the daemon: ```bash vllm preload --model nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16 \ --enforce-eager --max-model-len 4096 ``` Run the engine (`fallback: False`, so a disk fallback can't mask the result): ```python import os os.environ["VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING"] = "0" # in-process, so the model can be inspected from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams llm = LLM( model="nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16", load_format="ipc_cache", model_loader_extra_config={"fallback": False}, enforce_eager=True, max_model_len=4096, max_num_seqs=1, gpu_memory_utilization=0.5, ) out = llm.generate(["The capital of France is"], SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=24)) print(repr(out[0].outputs[0].text)) ``` Output: ```text [rank0]: RuntimeError: Triton Error [CUDA]: an illegal memory access was encountered [rank0]: torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered ``` The process then aborts (exit code 134). On smaller GPUs, `LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B` (~17 GB) reproduces the same way.
Minimal Reproducer (no GPU or model needed) ```python import torch from torch import nn class Gate(nn.Module): def __init__(self): super().__init__() self.e_score_correction_bias = nn.Parameter(torch.empty(4), requires_grad=False) class Router: # plain object, like GroupedTopKRouter def __init__(self, e_score_correction_bias): self.e_score_correction_bias = e_score_correction_bias def build(): with torch.device("meta"): gate = Gate() return gate, Router(gate.e_score_correction_bias) cached = torch.arange(4.0) # stands in for the daemon's tensor # What IpcModelLoader._apply_entries does today gate, router = build() gate._parameters.pop("e_score_correction_bias") gate.register_parameter("e_score_correction_bias", nn.Parameter(cached, requires_grad=False)) print("replace:", router.e_score_correction_bias.is_meta, router.e_score_correction_bias is gate.e_score_correction_bias) # Swapping in place keeps every holder on the same object gate, router = build() torch.utils.swap_tensors(gate.e_score_correction_bias, nn.Parameter(cached, requires_grad=False)) print("swap:", router.e_score_correction_bias.is_meta, router.e_score_correction_bias is gate.e_score_correction_bias) ``` ```text replace: True
