shortlist.title: [Onboarding 2026] Good first issues — start contributing to LMCache in one PR
shortlist.author: maobaolong
shortlist.body_excerpt:
👋 Welcome to join lmcache slack channel. https://join.slack.com/t/lmcacheworkspace/shared_invite/zt-4d1c2uk6t-55YZVvOQnJFNeAJK32U~Gg 

👋 Welcome to LMCache! This umbrella issue is the **single entry point** for first-time
contributors. If you've never sent a PR to LMCache before, start here.

> If you're looking for the older onboarding thread, see #627. This 2026 version
> focuses on smaller, well-scoped tasks with a friendly step-by-step PR workflow.

---

## 0. Before you start

- Read [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](../blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md). The most important parts:
  - Base branch is `dev`. Open PRs against `dev`, not `main`.
  - Every Python file starts with `# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0`.
  - Imports are grouped as `# Standard / # Third Party / # First Party / # Local`.
  - Line length is **88**, formatter is `ruff format`, lint is `ruff check`.
  - Never access `_private` members of other classes (SLF rule).
  - Public functions/methods need **type hints** + **docstring**.
- Set up the environment:
  ```bash
  uv venv --python 3.12 && source .venv/bin/activate
  uv pip install -e . --no-build-isolation
  uv pip install -r requirements/test.txt
  pre-commit install
  ```

## 1. How to claim a task

These tasks are mainly for new contributors to learn the LMCache issue-to-PR workflow. Please claim **only one good-first issue at a time**. If you already have an assigned good-first issue or an open good-first PR, finish that work before taking another one, and leave the remaining tasks for other newcomers.

1. Pick **one** sub-issue below that has no assignee and no `🔒 claimed` comment.
2. Comment exactly: `/claim` (or `I'd like to work on this 🙋`).
   A maintainer will assign it to you within ~2 business days.
3. If you go silent for 7 days we'll un-assign so others can pick it up — totally fine,
   just leave a comment if you need more time.

## 2. Branch & commit

```bash
git checkout dev && git pull
git checkout -b gfi/<issue-number>-short-slug
# ... do the work ...
git commit -s -m "short imperative summary"   # -s is required (DCO)
```

- **Sign-off is required** (`-s`). PRs without DCO sign-off cannot be merged.
- Keep the PR small: one issue = one PR.

## 3. Local checks (must pass before pushing)

```bash
pre-commit run --all-files
pytest -xvs tests/<the_file_you_touched>.py    # if applicable
```

## 4. Open the PR

**PR title format** (please follow):

```
[good-first-issue] <area>: <imperative summary>  (#<sub-issue-number>)
```

Examples:
- `[good-first-issue] docs: fix broken link in quickstart (#1801)`
- `[good-first-issue] tests: add unit test for FooBar.flush (#1802)`
- `[good-first-issue] lint: add SPDX header to scripts/foo.py (#1803)`

**PR description** — please use this template (the repo's PR template already
gives you the skeleton; just fill it in):

```markdown
**What this PR does / why we need it**:
Closes #<sub-issue-number>
Refs #<this umbrella issue number>

<one or two sentences describing the change>

**Special notes for your reviewers**:
- This is my first PR to LMCache 🙇 please be gentle.
- I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally — all green.
- I ran `pytest -xvs tests/...` — all green.

**If applicable**:
- [ ] this PR contains user facing changes - docs added
- [ ] this PR contains unit tests
```

> Tip: writing `Closes #1234` in the description auto-closes the sub-issue when the
> PR is merged. Keep `Refs #<umbrella>` so the umbrella stays linked.

## 5. Finding a reviewer

You don't need to find one yourself — `.github/CODEOWNERS` will auto-request
the right people based on the files you changed. If the PR sits idle for **3 working
days**, leave a polite comment like:

> Friendly ping — PTAL when you have a moment 🙏 cc @<one CODEOWNER from the file you changed>

If you really can't tell who to ping, default to:
- Tests / CI / packaging → @hickeyma @sammshen @ApostaC @deng451e
- Docs / examples → @sammshen @deng451e
- Storage backends → @maobaolong @sammshen @chunxiaozheng
- Core engine / memory → @ApostaC @YaoJiayi @sammshen
- Multiprocess → @ApostaC @OasisGit @hlin99

(See [`.github/CODEOWNERS`](../blob/dev/.github/CODEOWNERS) for the full map.)

## 6. Responding to review comments

This is the part most newcomers miss — please follow it, it makes everyone happier:

1. **Address every comment.** For each thread:
   - If you agree → push a fix and reply `Done in <commit-sha>`.
   - If you disagree → explain politely, propose an alternative.
   - If you don't understand → ask! Reviewers expect questions.
2. **Don't force-push** during review (it loses inline-comment context). Just add
   commits; we'll squash on merge.
3. **Re-request review explicitly** once all threads are resolved:
   > Addressed all comments, PTAL again 🙏 @reviewer1 @reviewer2

   `PTAL` = "Please Take Another Look". Tag every reviewer who left comments.
4. If CI is red, fix it before pinging — reviewers will skip red PRs.


---

## 7. How to create and claim a sub-issues

- You can extend the new cli commend line tools, ref to https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/pull/3719 and https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/pull/3678

---

Stuck? Drop a message in the `#contributors` channel of our
[Slack](https://join.slack.com/t/lmcacheworkspace/shared_invite/zt-3g8e6xzz8-KzS_HI8bPERGFK5PTB~MYg)
or comment here. We're happy to help. 🙌


**Maintainers**: please update this checklist as sub-issues are filed.

---

## Next step: Good second issues

Finished your first PR? Head over to **#5751 — [Good second issues — next step after your first PR](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/issues/5751)** for your next small, well-scoped task.

shortlist.title: llama-quantize: GGML_ASSERT(size mismatch) when quantizing mmproj files containing 3D conv tensors (gemma4v audio conv1d)
shortlist.author: mrBenBern
shortlist.body_excerpt:
Quantizing the gemma-4-E2B combined mmproj (vision+audio, gemma4v/gemma4a projectors) from F16 to Q8_0 aborts with:

  llama-quant.cpp:1365: GGML_ASSERT(gguf_get_tensor_size(...) == new_size) failed

Repro:
  llama-quantize --allow-requantize mmproj-F16.gguf out.gguf Q8_0

Fails at tensor `a.conv1d.0.weight` — shape [3,3,1,128] (3D conv1d from the audio encoder). The f32→f16 conversion changes the tensor size, and the split-output writer asserts on the mismatch. Every subsequent 3D tensor fails the same way (a.conv1d.1.weight [3,3,128,32], ...).

Workaround (verified): keep 3D tensors in f32 via tensor-type overrides —
  llama-quantize --allow-requantize \
    --tensor-type "a.conv1d.0.weight=f32" \
    --tensor-type "a.conv1d.1.weight=f32" \
    mmproj-F16.gguf mmproj-F16-q8_0.gguf Q8_0

This works and the resulting Q8_0 mmproj is functionally correct on-device (Android, llama.cpp 4ebdf2c): vision outputs verified same-in-quality as F16 (sign-text reading), encode on a Helio G99 CPU improved 6.4x vs BF16 (37s -> 5.8s for a 91-token image).

Expected behavior: either skip/conversion-preserving handling for N-D tensors whose element count doesn't allow requantization, or a clean error message listing the offending tensors instead of an assert.

shortlist.title: Performance comparison for dense shared prefix + block-diagonal local mask: custom mask in BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper vs MultiLevelCascadeAttentionWrapper
shortlist.author: catnanami
shortlist.body_excerpt: I am trying to evaluate the best way to implement an attention pattern with a dense shared/global prefix plus a local block-diagonal suffix. The mask pattern is shown below: I am considering two implementations: BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper with a custom mask MultiLevelCascadeAttentionWrapper Questions: 1. For this pattern, is cascade attention expected to be faster than paged prefill with a custom mask? 2. Or is this pattern better handled by a custom kernel/backend? My use case is speculative decoding, where all verification tokens share the same prefix KV, but each local block should only attend to its own block.

comments.author: VectorPeak
comments.body:
For the mask in the image - a dense shared prefix on the left plus independent block-diagonal local regions on the right - `MultiLevelCascadeAttentionWrapper` is usually the better fit than `BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper` with one large custom mask.

The reason is that the custom-mask prefill path does not really exploit this structure as well: it still treats the problem like one masked attention problem over the full layout, so the block-diagonal sparsity mostly becomes masking overhead. Cascade attention lets you model this as:

- shared/global prefix KV: attended by all verification tokens
- local suffix KV: split into independent blocks/requests
- final result: merge prefix-attention state with each local block’s attention state

For speculative decoding, this is exactly the kind of case where cascade can help, especially when the shared prefix is large and the local verification blocks are relatively small. Each local block can be represented as a separate batch item sharing the same prefix. If the local part also needs causal masking inside each block, use the normal causal/local mask for that per-block suffix attention.

I've dug into why this was dropped — \`Phi4FlashForCausalLM\` was removed in v0.10.2 during the V0 deprecation sweep because it explicitly declared \`SupportsV0Only\`, using the old \`MambaCacheManager\`/raw SSM ops plus a manual KV-cache-tensor hack for its YOCO cross-layer attention sharing.

Planned approach:
- Port the Mamba-1 layers to \`MambaMixer\` (\`vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/mamba_mixer.py\`), following the \`jamba.py\` pattern
- Replace the manual YOCO KV-sharing hack with the existing \`kv_sharing_target_layer_name\` primitive (used today by \`gemma3n.py\`) instead of reinventing cross-layer cache reuse
- Add the V1 cache-shape/dtype classmethods (\`get_mamba_state_shape_from_config\`, etc.) following Jamba
- Re-register the model and drop it from \`_PREVIOUSLY_SUPPORTED_MODELS\`

Will keep prefix-caching/chunked-prefill disabled for this model initially (matching the old V0 behavior) to scope a correctness-first first PR. Flagging the approach here in case a maintainer has opinions before I go deep — happy to adjust. Could I get this assigned?

shortlist.title: [Ascend Transport] Intermittent one-sided put failure (~2%): remote-buffer registration races transfer dispatch ("Can't find remoteBuffer", E19999 HcclBatchPut)
shortlist.author: yeshouxiaobai
shortlist.body_excerpt:
### Environment

- mooncake wheel: `mooncake-transfer-engine-npu 0.3.11.post1` (as shipped inside `quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0rc1-a3`)
- Hardware: 2× Atlas 800T A3 nodes, HCCS interconnect (16 NPU each)
- CANN 9.1.0, driver 26.0.rc1
- Use case: vLLM-Ascend PD disaggregation, AscendStore (mooncake backend) as an L2 KV pool — prefill workers put KV blocks into host-DRAM segments via `batch_put_from_multi_buffers`; 8 ranks per worker process, 32 segments total. Observed with both the shared global transfer engine and the store-independent TE path (`ASCEND_GLOBAL_RESOURCE_CONFIG` set); the P2P transfer engine (different connector, HBM-to-HBM one-sided reads) in the same process shows **zero** failures.

### Symptom

~2% of per-key puts fail with per-key error code `-1`. Engine-side log chain:

```text
E19999: Failed to invoke HcclBatchPut, hccl_result = 1 [comm_channel.cc:462]
  ... TransferSync ... remote_engine:192.168.x.x:20xxx, operation:write,
      op_descs size:22-24, timeout:30000 ms
client_service.cpp:1685] Transfer failed for key ...: TRANSFER_FAIL
client_service.cpp:1786] Successfully revoked failed put for key ...
(Worker) ERROR [mooncake_backend.py] Failed to put 1 keys out of 2. error_codes=[-1]
```

The real error is only visible in the CANN plog (`/root/ascend/log/debug/plog/`):

```text
[ERROR] HCCL(pid): [hccl_one_sided_conn.cc:364][GetTransInfo]
Can't find remoteBuffer by key[0x12e540000000][49152]
```

— i.e. the target host-DRAM buffer is not (yet) registered from the sender's perspective when the transfer dispatches. Same PID/thread, ~140µs before the E19999 line: directly causal.

### Evidence that this is an async-registration vs dispatch race

1. **Fails at zero concurrency**: first failure occurred during a single in-flight request (`Running: 0 reqs`) — not a load/resource-exhaustion issue.
2. **Uniform across targets**: failures spread evenly over all 32 remote segments (559–673 each over ~47 min) — not a port/binding/per-segment issue.
3. **Not idempotency/lease**: zero duplicate-key or lease errors; every failure is TRANSFER_FAIL.
4. **Small batches**: failing batches are 22–24 descriptors — not a descriptor overflow.
5. **Same-batch retries never recover; fresh dispatches do**: the transport's internal retry (same batch, ~300 ms apart, 3 attempts) fails every time; the next request that re-saves the same block (a fresh `batch_put_from_multi_buffers` call) succeeds. Consistent with the remote registration landing asynchronously *after* the raced dispatch.
6. **`ASCEND_THREAD_POOL_SIZE=1` makes it ~100% fatal** — the strongest signal. With the pool collapsed to a single thread, puts go from 98% success to near-total failure (only 2 keys stored; same key failing 6–7× back-to-back at 250 ms intervals): the blocking `TransferSync` starves the async registration task on the same `AscendThreadPool`. This strongly suggests remote-buffer registration is enqueued on the same pool that executes the sync transfer, and the two race under the default pool (~2% of the time).
7. Same remote address keeps failing in bursts over 18 minutes — a recurring race, not a one-shot boot-time problem.

### Attempted transport-level workarounds (both fail)

- `ASCEND_THREAD_POOL_SIZE=1` → livelock as above.
- `ASCEND_BUFFER_POOL=1` (adxl.BufferPool, would structurally bypass the per-allocation registration) → the *other* transfer engine in the same process (vLLM P2P connector via the global TE) then dies at boot: `adxl_engine_impl.cc:109 Failed to initialize AdxlEngine`. So BufferPool mode cannot be used when a P2P TE and a store TE coexist in one process.

### Current application-level mitigation

Re-issuing the failed key subset as a fresh `batch_put_from_multi_buffers` call (+50 ms / +200 ms) recovers the keys, which further confirms the async-registration model. We carry this as a patch on the vllm-ascend side (mooncake_backend.put re-issue loop) — but the race itself remains: the plog keeps logging `Can't find remoteBuffer` for every raced put.

### Ask

1. Make the one-sided put path self-consistent on Ascend: either resolve/register the remote buffer synchronously before dispatch, or have the in-batch retry re-resolve `remoteBuffer` instead of failing the whole task, or prioritize registration tasks over transfers on the shared pool.
2. Please document/consider making `ASCEND_BUFFER_POOL` coexist with a second (P2P) transfer engine in the same process — it looks like the intended structural fix but is unusable in mixed-TE deployments today.

Happy to share full logs (engine + plog), the repro workload, and the re-issue patch. Thanks!
